# NInfer for DeepSeek Harness

Manage local NInfer models and editable server profiles inside DSH. Includes the supplied Qwen3.8 27B 262k reference configuration.

## Install in DSH

Requires DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2**, running its Web profile.

1. Open **Plugins → Add plugin → GitHub**.
2. Paste `https://github.com/averyjohnkucan-arch/dsh-ninfer`.
3. Install and enable the plugin. Reload the browser, or restart DSH if its manager requests it.
4. Open **Settings → Models → NInfer**.

The plugin is a ready-to-install Cordis bundle. It does not patch DSH, replace its UI, install a second DSH, or require a plugin compilation step. Its package uses DSH's shipped peers, so installation does not download another provider stack or ask to run provider dependency build scripts.

## Models

Choose **Add model**, then **Select model files**. Browse the host's model directory and select multiple files, or **Select all model files here**. You can navigate between directories while retaining the selection. **Inspect and assign** reads headers and assigns the main model, its ordered shards, the vision projector and MTP. It reports missing shards, mixed main-model sets and unsupported MTP formats.

Edit the profile and save. **Start** prepares a missing runtime/model pack before starting the server. Runtime installation and model preparation show progress and can be cancelled. Existing installed engines and prepared packs can be selected under **Runtime and imported model data**. The model becomes available in DSH's conversation model picker after saving.

**Edit** reopens a saved profile. **Remove profile** deletes its saved configuration and stops its owned process; downloaded model files are retained. **Attach running server** explicitly connects to an already-running server advertising the profile's model ID. Stopping or disabling an attachment only detaches; it never terminates the external process. Launch settings are not applied to an external server.

All documented inference flags from the pinned executable's help have controls under **All engine CLI options**. Blank means the engine default; boolean **Omit flag** means the flag is not passed, not that an engine-default feature is necessarily disabled. The complete JSON editor supports repeated flags as arrays and multi-value flags as `{"argv":["first","second"]}`. Additional argv is an array, never a shell string. Environment variables and the complete server configuration are also editable.

## Updates, disable and removal

Update each repository independently through DSH's plugin manager. Turn its switch off to remove its card, provider registration and tools, and stop the servers it owns. Remove the bundle to uninstall its code. Saved profiles and runtime data remain in `~/.dsh/dsh-ninfer/` (or `$DSH_HOME/dsh-ninfer/`) so reinstalling restores them. Delete that plugin-owned data directory separately if you want a complete reset. Neither plugin requires the other.

## Integration

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and `dsh.client`; the patch inserts only its own Cordis row. The client registers React UI through the documented `settings.models.footer` slot and uses DSH theme tokens and locale service. The Host registers an `LlmAdapter` through `ctx.llm.registerAdapter`, delegates wire conversion, images and replay to DSH's public `PiAiAdapter`, and owns a separate `ctx.webServer.register` route. An ephemeral bearer capability supplied through `webserver/index-inject` protects its JSON actions. There is no iframe, DOM injection or replacement of built-in provider cards.

Registrations and process lifetimes are owned by `ctx.effect`/`ctx.on`. The agent-facing `ninfer_models` tool uses the same operations as the card and DSH's `approveEscalation` mechanism; host-management calls require Full access or explicit per-call approval. UI actions require the owner's page capability. This initial version targets the local Web profile; remote delegated access and Electron-only profiles have not been validated.

## Development

```sh
pnpm install --ignore-scripts
pnpm test
pnpm run check
```

Node 22.19+ is required. Development provider dependencies may report skipped optional install scripts; the published plugin has no install scripts and consumes DSH's installed peer packages. The two repositories contain their own code and tests and can be developed separately.

## NInfer runtime

Engine: [iamwavecut/ninfer-all](https://github.com/iamwavecut/ninfer-all), tested source revision `5ed86dff9fe3a5a0776f40a7aea86cf381da990d`.

The runtime installer builds the pinned upstream source with the engine patch shipped in `patches/ninfer-dflash-checkpoints.patch`. The patch adds native DFlash/DFlash2 disk snapshots, including draft-cache frontier metadata and reusable system-prefix anchors. It does not modify DSH. Existing profiles and binaries are not silently replaced.

Build prerequisites are Git, CMake 3.24+, Ninja, a compatible C++ compiler, CUDA 13.1 (including NVTX3 headers), and FFmpeg/cURL development packages. The default target is Linux x86_64 Blackwell `sm120a`. To select another supported GPU architecture or toolchain:

```sh
CMAKE=/path/to/cmake npm run build:checkpoints -- --root /path/to/runtime --arch 120a --jobs 8
```

`NINFER_CMAKE_ARGS` accepts a JSON array of additional CMake arguments. The build writes `checkpoint-build.json` with the upstream revision and patch hash. Select the resulting `build/apps/ninfer-serve` executable in the profile. The optional `scripts/fetch-ninfer.py` still fetches the pinned stock OCI binary; that stock binary does **not** support DFlash disk checkpoints. Model weights remain external.

NInfer consumes `.ninfer` artifacts. GGUF-to-NInfer conversion is not implemented by this plugin. NInfer's server flags, calibration action, environment and optional temporary power-profile hold are exposed. Calibration is user-triggered and saves its profile path. There is no automatic tuning in this plugin.

## Included Qwen3.8 27B reference profile

The initial profile preserves the owner's supplied setup:

```text
--max-context 262144 --kv-capacity 262144 --max-concurrency 1
--kv-dtype rk4v4 --spec dflash2 --draft-tokens 7 --lm-head-draft
--embedding-q4 --gdn-state-fp16 --prefill-cublas --prefill-chunk 512
--ngram-draft-tokens 0
```

It uses model ID `qwen3.8-27b`, port 8188, text-only input, a performance power-profile hold, and the supplied environment/calibration paths. The owner's absolute paths are an editable reference; other installations must select their own downloaded artifact and runtime libraries.

Model: [neroued/Qwen3.8-27B-NInfer](https://huggingface.co/neroued/Qwen3.8-27B-NInfer), revision `1cbd84e7221e51186bd7f093a149912d2489625b`, supplied SHA-256 `81f924d440c27261d820c19a9f8d45794c5aee410f8a68bd358133fa8c0375da`.

The reported benchmark numbers belong to the owner's prior run and are not claimed as a new plugin benchmark. No model inference or calibration was rerun while importing this profile. Reinstalling the plugin retains edited profiles; the seed is created only when no profile store exists.

When Start or a chat finds an existing server on the saved port, it automatically reuses it only if `/v1/models` advertises the exact saved model ID. The plugin never takes ownership of that process: Stop detaches, and saved launch changes require restarting the external server yourself. A different model, an invalid response, or an authenticated server without matching credentials is rejected. Strata tuning requires a plugin-owned server and never reuses an external process.

## Per-model reasoning settings

Edit a model profile to add/remove reasoning levels, give each a display name,
and set the exact `reasoning_effort` backend value. Choose a default level, or
Engine default to leave the request unspecified. Custom names and values are
supported; availability is declared per profile, not assumed for every model.
The engine/template must accept the configured backend values.

Qwen3.8 profiles start with Off (thinking disabled), Low → `low`, Medium → `medium`, and XHigh → `xhigh`,
with Medium as default. The conversation model picker uses these profile-owned
settings through DSH's existing adapter reasoning metadata. No DSH core patch
is required. An empty level list hides the reasoning selector for that profile.

## Model Scheduler integration

Optionally install `dsh-model-scheduler` for shared GPU admission, queued chat switching, manual load/unload and separate configurable idle retention (five minutes by default) and switch grace (30 seconds by default). This provider remains independently usable. Scheduling policy lives in that separate Cordis service; no Harness core changes are required. Owned engine process groups are stopped before GPU release is reported. External servers are detached, never killed.

## Per-chat checkpoints and shared prefixes

The per-profile **Keep model loaded while idle** setting (`keepWarm: true`) preserves the running engine and its in-memory cache when the optional Model Scheduler is installed. Another queued model, image job, manual Unload or shutdown can still release it. Other profiles retain their normal idle timer.

For the qualified Qwen3.8 profile, `cacheStableHistory: true` enables positional system and tool updates through the public provider adapter. It requires `--chat-template` to point to this plugin's `assets/qwen3_8-cache.jinja` and `--preserve-thinking: true`. The external template derives from the pinned upstream Qwen3.8 template; stock NInfer remains unchanged. Tool declarations stay at their history positions while the full catalog remains available to the server for tool validation.

This processes new user text after Send. It does not process drafts or generate background answers. Changing the template requires a one-time cache rebuild. Cold loads, history edits, compaction, reasoning changes and non-additive tool changes can still require recomputation. Do not enable this template on unrelated model families without validation.

With the patched engine selected, enable **Save per-chat KV checkpoints**. The provider serializes restore → inference → save through its official DSH adapter. Every successfully completed inference step (including tool calls and token-limit stops) publishes a durable native checkpoint. Interrupted or failed steps retain the preceding valid checkpoint. Each chat retains its two most recently used model configurations. Auxiliary summarization/title calls and externally attached servers do not write checkpoints.

Checkpoints live in the plugin data directory under `kv/chats/`, with hashed chat IDs, private file permissions, atomic manifests, and compatibility fingerprints covering weights, executable and launch settings. Their contents include conversation state; treat this directory as private chat data. A missing, incompatible or corrupt checkpoint falls back to normal prefill and exposes a warning in model status.

When switching chats, the provider first checks for a compatible continuation still resident in the native GPU/host cache. Otherwise it restores a snapshot from disk. Fresh chats use an independent base checkpoint under `kv/bases/`, keyed to the model and exact system/tool/rendering configuration. It survives eviction of chat snapshots. A new configuration is warmed once using the system/tools, a blank synthetic user message and one discarded token (the native APIs require generation to retain state). No real user or assistant history enters that seed. Native prefix anchors limit reuse to the matching system/tool tokens before the real user message. Subsequent chats restore this base without rebuilding it. Existing chats always prefer their own latest checkpoint. Legacy cross-chat reuse remains a fallback when no independent base exists. Edits and compaction recompute from the last compatible native anchor, which may precede the exact edit position.

The patch uses NInfer's original checkpoint catalog (`--slot-save-path`), because its alternate hybrid cache does not expose native snapshots. The plugin manages that directory and rejects conflicting cache flags. It defaults to eight private anchors per continuation and an 8 GiB host-cache budget; explicit profile values take precedence. Smaller budgets can fail startup when the recurrent-state images exceed the engine's allocation limit. This path can have different memory/performance characteristics from stock DFlash2 caching. Snapshots are native full snapshots, not incremental deltas; long contexts can require substantial disk space and write bandwidth. Same-model resident reuse avoids reloading weights, but disk transfers and different-model loads are not guaranteed to finish in one or two seconds. See [measured checkpoint validation](docs/CHECKPOINT-VALIDATION.md) for the tested configuration and limitations.

The **Off** reasoning level disables thinking with `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false`; it does not send the literal `off` as an unsupported reasoning-effort value. Existing version-1 model profiles gain Off once on upgrade; custom names and Medium defaults are preserved. Set a custom row's backend value to `off` for the same behavior.

To qualify the native checkpoint path on your model, start a managed checkpoint-enabled server and run `python3 scripts/verify-checkpoints.py capture --url http://127.0.0.1:PORT --model MODEL --report REPORT.json`. Restart that server, run the same command with `restore`, then restart and run it with `cold`. The script compares restored continuation against uninterrupted greedy output, checks actual native cached-token counts, and compares shared-prefix reuse against a cold new chat. It writes one test snapshot named `dsh-qualification.kv`; use a dedicated test profile. This requires real model weights and GPU access; the ordinary plugin tests do not substitute for it.

## Portable engine installation

Fresh installs begin without saved machine-specific profiles. Import your local `.ninfer` weights, then use engine setup for that profile. Existing saved profiles are preserved. The engine patch is bundled and verified against a pinned source revision and full resulting source tree; new builds use separate revision/patch directories. See [NVFP4 and KV engine installation](docs/nvfp4-kv-engine.md) for supported controls, prerequisites and current qualification limits.

## Recommended models and verified downloads

Open **Recommended models · exact revisions and hashes** in this plugin's settings card. The catalog records the checkpoints/components from the owner's configured setup with immutable repository revisions and SHA-256 (or Git blob hashes for small snapshot assets). Expand **Files, sizes and exact identities** before selecting a set.

**Download / verify recommended** saves a complete pinned set in this plugin's private `recommended-models` directory. Downloads resume from partial files, validate content before publishing final files, preserve existing models, and expose progress, cancellation and explicit failures. Repeating the action verifies/reuses existing files. Downloads do not start inference. **Add downloaded files** fills the existing model import/edit workflow for review and saving. Runtime installation remains separate.

Some configured artifacts are locally converted or assembled from multiple sources. Their exact local hashes are listed, but downloading the original publisher checkpoint cannot recreate those bytes. Use **Add existing model** and the normal importer for those entries. No incomplete component set is presented as a working download. Recommendations describe the saved setup; they do not establish memory fit or model quality on another computer.

Existing retained catalog snapshots are not re-certified or replaced by this duplicate decision.

# dsh-usage · Token Usage Breakdown, API Balance & Cost Monitor for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) English | [中文](README.zh.md)

   

Token Usage Breakdown, Multi-Provider Balance & Cost Monitor for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)
Daily Token Analytics · Provider API Balance · Subscription Quotas · Peak/Off-Peak Costing · Token Bank

A dedicated token usage and cost monitoring plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI and official desktop client: multi-provider balances, coding subscription quota tracking, live token accounting ledgers, and a compact quick-glance card above settings in the sidebar. ## What it does The plugin runs a host-side service and a first-level settings section (使用统计, directly below the Workshop entry): - **Usage tab (用量)**: today's token totals per bucket (input / output / cache read / cache write, disjoint as the provider reports them) with per-provider and per-model breakdown, the last 30 days as a horizontal provider/model bar chart, and the balance of every configured provider (one row per adapter family: a dormant catalog alias shadowed by the family's live route no longer renders its own balance row). A **day picker** switches that card to any retained day that recorded usage (today first, then the other days newest first) and the card then shows that day's own totals, provider rows, and estimated spend; the peak/off-peak line stays on today because it describes the pricing window now. The ledger folds live `session/event` streams (`request/header` route attribution plus `assistant/message` usage) into `$DSH_HOME/dsh-usage/usage-ledger.json` with day-based retention, so past days survive restarts; counting starts when the plugin is first enabled. For the official DeepSeek family the tab also shows the current peak/off-peak pricing period (Beijing weekdays 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00 are peak, billed at double) and today's estimated spend in CNY. - **Plans tab (个人套餐)**: coding-plan quota windows for every configured provider that exposes one — used percent and reset time per window (Kimi For Coding 5h/week, GLM Coding Plan 5h/week/month, OpenCode Go rolling/weekly/monthly, MiniMax 5h/week, Codex / ChatGPT subscription 5h/week). Providers without a real plan or subscription (DeepSeek, ZenMux, Moonshot, OpenRouter, SiliconFlow) never appear on this tab; their balance shows on the usage tab instead. - **Token Bank tab (Token 银行)**: the whale-yuan voucher (鲸元券) minted from the official DeepSeek family's ledger at an anti-inflation exchange rate of 1,000,000 tokens per whale yuan. The tab sums the family's retained-ledger tokens (the `deepseek` catalog alias and the live `deepseek-official` route combined), stamps the minted face value onto the banknote artwork with a serial line carrying the minting window, and offers a save-image button plus a native share button when the browser supports sharing files. The spend line shows the real CNY total observed from the official balance once available — balance decreases accrue as spend, top-ups never count — and falls back to the fold-time estimate before the first observation. The minted total prefers the host's whole-ledger aggregate and falls back to the last 30 days on an older host; with no official DeepSeek usage the tab shows its empty state. A day picker mints the note from one picked day instead of the whole retention window (the observed-spend line, which accrues from the first balance reading, is whole-window only and falls back to that day's fold-time estimate on a single day). The on-note text is locale-neutral (digits, latin captions, ISO dates) and the export is rendered locally in the browser. - **Sidebar foot card**: a compact glance seated above the sidebar's Settings row — today's estimated spend as the headline (today's tokens when nothing priced is recorded yet), the tokens/calls line, and up to two configured-provider balances with a +N overflow. The whole card is one button that opens the usage settings section, so detail stays in one place, and the corner chevron folds it into a one-line strip (the spending provider's name, the label, and the headline value), a choice persisted across reloads. It polls at a relaxed 30 s cadence while the tab is visible, hides in the collapsed 56 px rail, and disappears while the plugin is disabled. - Probes run entirely host-side on a poll cycle (default 60 s, manual refresh button); API keys are resolved through the harness credential seam (`llm-pi-ai` records, `apiKeyEnv` references) and never reach the browser. Supported balance endpoints: DeepSeek (the official live route `deepseek-official` and the catalog alias `deepseek` both resolve), Moonshot (CN/international), OpenRouter, SiliconFlow (CN/international), ZenMux. Supported plan endpoints: Kimi For Coding, GLM Coding Plan (CN via open.bigmodel.cn, international via api.z.ai — the `zai` route the pi-ai catalog registers, plus the `zai-coding` / `zai-coding-cn` aliases; 5-hour, weekly and monthly windows, token-metered and credit-metered plans), OpenCode Go, MiniMax, Codex / ChatGPT subscription (OAuth access token from the pi-ai grant; a stale token shows an error until the harness next refreshes it). Providers without a programmatic endpoint (Qwen token plans, OpenCode Zen PAYG, Anthropic, OpenAI) are listed without facts. ### Spend estimate scope Today's spend is an estimate priced at fold time from the published DeepSeek peak/off-peak price book (CNY per million tokens; peak = the windows above, off-peak half of peak). The rows in force are `deepseek-flash` (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) and `deepseek-v4-pro`: the retired flash ids (`deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) bill the flash row, and `deepseek-v4-pro` moves to that row once DeepSeek routes the id to V4.1-Flash on 2026-09-14 12:00 Beijing. It covers the official DeepSeek routes only — relay traffic billed elsewhere (ZenMux, SiliconFlow, ...) stays unpriced — and unknown DeepSeek model ids take the flash-class row. Buckets recorded before a price change keep the old pricing, so a price-book update is reflected from the moment it ships, not retroactively. The published rule bills a Chinese public holiday entirely off-peak even on a Monday-Friday, and bills an adjusted workday falling on a Saturday or Sunday off-peak too. Weekends are therefore already off-peak by construction, and this package ships the State Council holiday table (`src/core/holidays.ts`, 2020 through 2026, taken from the MIT-licensed [chinese-holidays-node](https://github.com/bastengao/chinese-holidays-node) yearly data with only its `holiday` entries), so a public-holiday weekday is estimated at the off-peak row instead of reading up to about twice the real spend. A year the table does not cover (later than 2026) falls back to the published windows, which reads high rather than low — the safer direction to be wrong in. ## Install Requires DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 or later: the plugin is developed against the 0.2.1-rc.2 DSH cohort (its settings page is the Host-generated page of the plugin's own Config schema) and its `@deepseek-ai/*` runtime imports are provided by the host itself. In your profile (e.g. `~/.dsh/profiles/web`): ```bash pnpm add @linxin666/dsh-usage ``` and insert into `cordis.patch.yml` (or use the bundle patch): ```yaml - insert: - id: usage name: '@linxin666/dsh-usage' ``` Restart `dsh web` for the host half; the client half applies on refresh. The section lives in `Settings -> Usage Statistics`. ## Configuration | Key | Default | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `enabled` | `true` | Master switch; off = no listeners, no probes, no routes | | `pollIntervalSec` | `60` | Provider probe cycle (30-3600 s; a change reloads the plugin row) | | `retainDays` | `180` | Ledger retention in local days (7-730) | ## Known limitations - Usage counting starts when the plugin is first enabled; historical sessions are not backfilled. - OAuth-based routes (for example qwen OAuth grants) are detected as such but not probed; the plugin does not spend third-party OAuth budgets. - A failed probe keeps the previous fact visible and reports the error line; providers may rate-limit aggressive polling. - The voucher's face value covers the ledger's retention window (`retainDays`): pruned days drop out of both the trend chart and the note. - The day pickers list only days the ledger recorded usage on: a day without usage is never offered, and a day pruned by retention leaves an empty or zeroed card rather than a different one. - The real-spend watch starts at the first official balance observation: earlier consumption is not backfilled, and only observed balance decreases accrue (a balance rise is a top-up and never counts). # @linxin666/dsh-usage DSH Web GUI 的用量统计插件:按 provider 记录 token 账本、探测余额与编码套餐额度,并在侧栏 Settings 上方放一张紧凑的价格速览卡。 Usage statistics plugin for the DSH web GUI: per-provider balance and coding-plan quota detection plus a live token usage ledger, with a compact price glance card above the sidebar's Settings row. > 双语说明:每一节先中文、后英文,两种语言都能独立读完。 > Bilingual on purpose: each section gives the Chinese text first, then the English text; either half reads on its own. ![使用统计面板(今日视图) · The usage panel, today view](preview/final-today.png) --- ## 简介 · Overview ### 中文 `dsh-usage` 是 DeepSeek Harness(DSH)的用量统计插件。本仓库包含它的源码、构建产物与测试脚本,并在上游@linxin666/dsh-usage 0.4.8 之上做了四类增强: 1. **使用统计面板重做**(浏览器半边 `lib/client.js`)——8 个统计窗口、6 格汇总、趋势图、按渠道/按模型的彩色拆分,详见下文「特性」。 2. **会话日志回填**(host 半边 `lib/index.js`)——插件挂载之前发生的用量,从会话日志补读回来;由 `src/` 直接构建。 3. **多设备账本**——每台机器写自己的 `usage-ledger..json`,总览相加所有设备;账本可导出/导入,导入是替换而非合并,同一文件导入两次不会重复计数。详见 [`docs/multi-device.md`](docs/multi-device.md)。 4. **上游 0.4.8 合并**——DeepSeek 峰谷价标签;识别反向代理的 loopback 校验(`isProxiedRequest()`):带 `x-forwarded-for` 或 `cf-connecting-ip` 的请求不再被当作本机直连,堵住 GUI 挂在反代后面的鉴权绕过。 基线是 npm 上正式发布的 **0.4.8**(本地合并,不是上游 fork)。 ### English `dsh-usage` is the usage-statistics plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). This repository holds its sources, build output and test harnesses, plus four groups of enhancements on top of upstream 0.4.8: 1. **A redesigned usage panel** (browser half, `lib/client.js`) — eight statistic windows, a six-cell totals row, a trend chart and a colour-coded channel/model breakdown; see Features below. 2. **Session-log backfill** (host half, `lib/index.js`) — usage that happened before the plugin mounted is read back from the session logs; built straight from `src/`. 3. **Multi-device ledgers** — each machine writes its own `usage-ledger..json` and the overview sums every device; ledgers can be exported and imported, and importing replaces (never merges), so the same file cannot double-count. See [`docs/multi-device.md`](docs/multi-device.md). 4. **Upstream 0.4.8 merge** — the DeepSeek peak/off-peak badge, and a proxy-aware loopback guard (`isProxiedRequest()`): requests carrying `x-forwarded-for` or `cf-connecting-ip` no longer count as loopback, which closes an auth bypass when the GUI sits behind a reverse proxy. The baseline is the published npm release **0.4.8** (merged locally; not a fork of the upstream repo). --- ## 特性 · Features ### 中文 以下是面板这边的核心特性。 **8 个统计窗口。** 今日、昨日、近 3 天、近 7 天、近 30 天、近 6 个月、全部、自定义。45 天以内按天累加;更长的窗口(近 6 个月、全部、超 45 天的自定义)由一次 `GET /api/dsh-usage/range` 聚合查询给出,半年视图不必再逐天抓两百次。 **6 格汇总,回答「缓存到底值不值」。** 总 tokens、输入、输出、缓存读、缓存命中率、调用次数。命中率 = `cacheRead / (input + cacheRead + cacheWrite)`——判断 prompt 缓存是否划算,看的就是这个数。 **长窗口友好的趋势图。** `TrendChart` 分桶:≤45 天按天、46–200 天按周、更长按月;网格线取 1/2/5×10ⁿ;悬浮提示给出总量、调用次数、命中率与前三名模型;没有记录的日子明确标注「无记录」。 **一个模型一种颜色,到处一致。** 颜色由归一化模型名的稳定哈希在 16 色色板上取位得到,同一个模型在趋势图、渠道条、模型子条、图例和悬浮提示里都是同一种颜色;只差大小写或 `provider/` 前缀的写法(`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` 与 `deepseek-v4.1-flash`)会归一成同一个模型,而不是拆成两种颜色。 **拆分列出每一个模型,不只是前三名。** 每个渠道先画一条按模型堆叠的条,再逐行列出 host 返回的每一个模型(协议单渠道上限 12 行),每行一条同色子条。渠道条以**窗口总量**为分母,长度就是渠道在窗口里的占比;模型子条以**自己的渠道**为分母,读起来就是「这个渠道怎么分」。渠道行用更重的字重,模型行整体压暗一档,两个层级一眼能分开。 **从侧栏一步到面板。** 点侧栏底部的用量卡,直接打开「设置 · 使用统计」,不用再走账号菜单。实现是请 shell 的 registry 打开设置页(合成一次 Ctrl+, 按键,这是平台的默认快捷键);500 ms 内面板没出现,才退回账号菜单那条路。 ### English The panel-side features at a glance: **Eight statistic windows.** Today, Yesterday, Last 3 days, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 6 months, All time, Custom (the UI shows these labels in Chinese). Windows up to 45 days are summed day by day; anything longer — all time, or a custom range past 45 days — is answered by one `GET /api/dsh-usage/range` aggregate, so a six-month view no longer has to fetch two hundred days one at a time. **A six-cell totals row that answers the cache question.** Total tokens, input, output, cache read, cache-hit ratio and calls, where the ratio is `cacheRead / (input + cacheRead + cacheWrite)` — the number to look at when judging whether prompt caching pays for itself. **A trend chart that survives long windows.** `TrendChart` buckets daily up to 45 days, weekly from 46 to 200, monthly beyond that; gridlines follow the 1/2/5×10ⁿ steps; the hover tooltip shows totals, calls, the hit ratio and the top three models; days with nothing recorded say so explicitly. **One colour per model, everywhere.** Colours come from a stable hash of the normalized model name over a sixteen-hue palette, so a model keeps a single hue across the trend chart, the channel bars, the model rows, the legend and the tooltip. Spellings that differ only by letter case or by a `provider/` prefix (`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` vs `deepseek-v4.1-flash`) fold into one model instead of splitting into two colours. **A breakdown that lists every model, not just the top three.** Each channel draws one bar stacked by its models, then lists every model the host returned (the wire caps a provider at twelve rows) with a sub-bar in the same hue. The channel bar measures against the window total, so its length is the channel's share of the window; the model sub-bars measure against their own channel, so they read as how that channel splits. The channel header carries the heavier type and the sub-rows sit one step lighter, which keeps the two levels apart at a glance. **One click from the sidebar to the panel.** Clicking the usage card at the bottom of the sidebar opens the usage-statistics settings page directly instead of going through the account menu. It asks the shell's registry to open the page (a synthetic Ctrl+, keydown, the platform default) and falls back to the account-menu path only if the page has not appeared within 500 ms. --- ## 快速开始 · Quick start ### 中文 环境要求:Node `^22.19.0` 或 `>=24.0.0`,DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.2`,React `^18.2.0`(peer)。许可证 Apache-2.0。 ```bash pnpm install --frozen-lockfile # 从 pnpm-lock.yaml 装工具链 cd packages/dsh-usage && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsc -b tsconfig.build.json \ && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsdown # 构建(~100 ms,exit 0) cd ../.. && node harness/build-test-bundle.cjs && node harness/render-test.mjs node --experimental-strip-types harness/host-test.mjs ``` 期望输出:`=== 185/185 checks passed ===` 和 `=== 214/214 checks passed ===`。`node_modules/` 已被 git 忽略,新克隆的仓库要先装依赖;构建能逐字节复现已提交的产物。 ### English Requirements: Node `^22.19.0` or `>=24.0.0`, DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.2`, React `^18.2.0` (peer). []; for (const packageName of bundles) { /* resolve, read dsh.bundle.patch, load */ } ``` 插件管理器和插件市场两条路会自动登记;手工 `pnpm add` 只做了第 1 步,所以要补上: ```bash node -e ' const fs = require("fs"); const p = "package.json"; const m = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(p, "utf8")); m.dsh ??= {}; m.dsh.profile ??= {}; const b = m.dsh.profile.bundles ??= []; if (!b.includes("@linxin666/dsh-usage")) { b.push("@linxin666/dsh-usage"); fs.writeFileSync(p, JSON.stringify(m, null, 2) + "\n"); console.log("added to dsh.profile.bundles"); } else console.log("already in dsh.profile.bundles"); ' ``` 然后**重启 DSH**:host bundle 在启动时一次性进 ESM 图,新的 host 路由必须重启(只改客户端半边的话,刷新页面即可)。 **踩坑清单:** - `#path:/packages/dsh-usage` 必填——插件在仓库的子目录里,不在根目录。 - 离线机器可改用本地克隆:`git+file:///E:/path/to/dsh-usage/.git#path:/packages/dsh-usage`;目录本身不是 git checkout 时用 `file:E:/path/to/dsh-usage/packages/dsh-usage`。POSIX 风格路径的 `file:` 会报 `ERR_PNPM_LINKED_PKG_DIR_NOT_FOUND`,Windows 上要传 Windows 路径(`cygpath -w`)。 - pnpm 会把 git 依赖解析成钉住 commit 的 codeload tarball(`pnpm-lock.yaml` 里形如 `…/tar.gz/#path:/packages/dsh-usage`),装出来是一份**真拷贝,不是链接**:好处是别的插件再也覆盖不掉,坏处是**新提交不会自己过来**——推完之后重跑一次 `pnpm add`(或 `pnpm update @linxin666/dsh-usage`)。 - `hoisted` linker 下改 `src/` 不会更新已安装的机器:重新构建、提交、再跑一次 `pnpm add`。 - 命令以 `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`(koffi、node-pty、protobufjs……)收尾是 profile 既有的噪声,不是失败。装好后用 `patches/audit-store.sh` 加下面的哈希表验证;树已经来自本仓库,`patches/install-patches.sh` 不再需要。 ### English Two steps: install the package into the profile, then register it in `dsh.profile.bundles`. **Step 1 — install.** Profiles normally pin this package to a registry version, and any other plugin's install, update or removal re-resolves that pin and **overwrites the copy**. Pointing the profile at a git dependency pins the commit instead and makes the copy stable: ```bash cd "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles/desktop" pnpm remove @linxin666/dsh-usage pnpm add "github:beici/dsh-usage-for-personal-use#path:/packages/dsh-usage" ``` **Step 2 — register the bundle.** The host builds its patch layers from the `dsh.profile.bundles` list, not from `node_modules` — a package that is installed but absent from the list is simply never loaded: no patch layer, no routes, no panel: ```js // loadProfileDirectory() in the DSH host const bundles = readProfileManifest(binName, dir).dsh?.profile?.bundles ?? []; for (const packageName of bundles) { /* resolve, read dsh.bundle.patch, load */ } ``` The plugin manager and the plugin market register the bundle for you; a bare `pnpm add` does not, so add it by hand: ```bash node -e ' const fs = require("fs"); const p = "package.json"; const m = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(p, "utf8")); m.dsh ??= {}; m.dsh.profile ??= {}; const b = m.dsh.profile.bundles ??= []; if (!b.includes("@linxin666/dsh-usage")) { b.push("@linxin666/dsh-usage"); fs.writeFileSync(p, JSON.stringify(m, null, 2) + "\n"); console.log("added to dsh.profile.bundles"); } else console.log("already in dsh.profile.bundles"); ' ``` Then **restart DSH**: the host bundle joins the ESM graph once at boot, so new host routes need a restart (client-only changes reload on page refresh). **Pitfalls:** - `#path:/packages/dsh-usage` is required — the plugin lives in a subdirectory of the repository, not at its root. - On a machine without network access to the remote, use a local clone: `git+file:///E:/path/to/dsh-usage/.git#path:/packages/dsh-usage`; for a plain directory that is not a git checkout, `file:E:/path/to/dsh-usage/packages/dsh-usage`. A POSIX-style path with `file:` fails (`ERR_PNPM_LINKED_PKG_DIR_NOT_FOUND`) — pass a Windows path (`cygpath -w`) on Windows. - pnpm resolves the git dependency to a commit-pinned codeload tarball (`…/tar.gz/#path:/packages/dsh-usage` in `pnpm-lock.yaml`), so the installed tree is a **real copy, not a link**: other plugins can no longer overwrite it, but **new commits do not arrive by themselves** — re-run `pnpm add` (or `pnpm update @linxin666/dsh-usage`) after pushing. - Under the `hoisted` linker, editing `src/` does not update an installed machine: rebuild, commit, run `pnpm add` again. - Ending with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` (koffi, node-pty, protobufjs, ...) is pre-existing profile noise, not a failure. # Bookmark Research

**English** · [中文](README.zh.md)

[![GitHub Bookmark-Canvas](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Bookmark--Canvas-181717?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Browser-bookmark-hub/Bookmark-Canvas)
[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/bookmark-research?logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bookmark-research)

Research with bookmark context and retain reusable knowledge. Read a [Bookmark Canvas](https://github.com/Browser-bookmark-hub/Bookmark-Canvas) package, investigate with the host model or a research API, and save sourced Wiki pages. Works in **Codex, Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness (dsh)**.

[Installation guide](docs/installation.en.md) · [User guide](docs/user-guide.en.md) · [Details](docs/details.en.md) · [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bookmark-research)

## How it works

- **Local understanding.** A Bookmark Canvas package is read as structure, not a flat URL list: card and group layout, edges with their direction and labels, and the same bookmark appearing across cards (spatial context); dated fields, protocol-defined date segments in IDs, and Git commits that changed content (temporal context). These queries run offline.
- **External research takes one of three routes.** Reading a known URL needs no reasoning; agentic search has the host model plan, search, read and follow the gaps; deep research can use the OpenAI or Parallel research API directly. Persistent inventories and coverage checks are available when you explicitly need a complete collection audit. Host browsers and crawlers can supply source text.
- **Reviewed knowledge store.** Finished research can be compiled into a Wiki of reviewed pages with revisions and links, reused by later questions instead of searching the web again.

## Requirements

- Python 3.9+ with SQLite FTS5 (checked by `bookmark-research doctor`)
- The CLI of at least one client: Codex, Claude Code or DeepSeek Harness (dsh). DeepSeek Harness (dsh) also needs `pnpm`, unless it is the DeepSeek Harness Desktop CLI, which carries its own
- Node 18+ and npm to install a release
- No API key is needed to install, or to query bookmarks locally

## Install

```sh
npx bookmark-research install
```

Installs the latest version directly. Add `--lang zh` for the Chinese wizard. For a permanent command, run `npm install -g bookmark-research`; the GitHub convenience script uses the same npm release (macOS/Linux/WSL):

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Browser-bookmark-hub/Bookmark-Research/main/install.sh | bash
```

### What the installer asks

1. **Clients** — arrow keys and Space to toggle; detected CLIs are preselected. The install plan is shown for confirmation.
2. **Research depth (optional)** — leave `auto` and the depth is picked from each request; set `quick`, `agentic` or `deep` only to pin one default.
3. **Answer and report language** — follow the question, Chinese or English.
4. **Search and page-reading services** — one ordered multiselect. Unselected providers become the fallback search tier.
5. **Storage** — the default data folder, one custom folder for archives and reports, or reports beside the bookmark file or folder.
6. **Optional professional APIs** — off by default: OpenAI Deep Research or the Parallel Task API.
7. **API keys** — one hidden prompt per selected key, checked immediately; every key is optional.
8. **Service check** — runs on its own and reports each provider; a sample search/read test is opt-in.

Enter keeps the highlighted value, so a full run can be just a few keystrokes. Then start a new client session so the Skill and MCP tools load. Wiki follow-up suggests retention and honors existing authorization. Optional service diagnostics retain a 15-minute cache.

### Non-interactive install

| Client | Command | Registers with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex | `npx bookmark-research install codex --non-interactive` | `codex plugin add` |
| Claude Code | `npx bookmark-research install claude --scope user --non-interactive` | `claude plugin install` |
| DeepSeek Harness (dsh) | `npx bookmark-research install dsh --profile web --non-interactive` | `dsh plugin add` |

Several at once: `npx bookmark-research install claude dsh --profile web --non-interactive`. Project scope: `--scope project --project /path/to/project` (Claude Code). All options: [installation guide](docs/installation.en.md).

**Ask your agent to install it.** Paste this into Codex, Claude Code or DeepSeek Harness (dsh):

```text
Install the Bookmark Research plugin into the client you are running in.

1. Identify your own client: codex, claude or dsh.
2. Run: npx bookmark-research install <client> --non-interactive
   - Claude Code: add --scope user (or --scope project --project <dir>).
   - DeepSeek Harness (dsh): add --profile <profile>; ask me for the profile name.
3. The command prints JSON. Confirm "verified": true and report any "error".
4. Do not ask me for API keys in chat. Tell me to run `bookmark-research setup`
   in my terminal to enter them.
5. Tell me to start a new session so the Skill and MCP tools load.
```

Install notes:

- **npm is the single release source** for all three hosts; it contains the shared runtime, Skill and host adapters. The installer downloads the release, prepares the host's format, then calls the host's native commands. GitHub hosts source, versions and the installation catalog; unpublished source uses the Python installer. See [distribution policy](docs/distribution.md).
- **DeepSeek Harness (dsh) installs the release directly.** The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin --profile <name> add bookmark-research@<version>` installs it with no export first. The reserved `desktop` profile belongs to DeepSeek Harness Desktop; use that app's CLI, which the installer and wizard locate themselves.
- **Windows** often has no working `python3`, so the installer writes the detected Python path into each client's MCP config. Install Codex with `bookmark-research install codex` rather than adding the repository to Codex directly; `bookmark-research status` shows the interpreter in use.

## Configure and update

**Open the configuration page.** Run `bookmark-research` with no arguments in a terminal: the menu covers preferences and API keys, service checks, installing into another client, updates and status. The alias `bookmark` (or `bookmark research`) does the same, and `bookmark-research setup` goes straight to the wizard.

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Preferences and API keys | `bookmark-research setup` |
| Menu | `bookmark-research` · `bookmark` · `bookmark research` |
| Clients, preferences, storage, recent research, key status | `bookmark-research status` |
| Scripted preferences | `bookmark-research config show` · `bookmark-research config set --input prefs.json` |
| Update or verify all clients | `bookmark-research update` · `bookmark-research verify` |

Use `npx bookmark-research …` if the command is not installed globally. Preferences and keys are user-wide, so one change applies to every installed client; start a new client session afterwards. `--lang zh` shows the wizard and menu in Chinese. The default `quick` preset exposes 21 everyday tools. Use `bookmark-research config set --tool-scope-preset deep` for the full 43-tool catalog when a persistent collection audit is needed. An explicit `tool_scope` list still overrides the preset.

**Update.** `bookmark-research update` refreshes every installed client from its registered source and keeps preferences, keys and data. Re-running `npx bookmark-research install` or `bookmark-research update` also upgrades existing installations in place (including Codex, Claude Code, and DeepSeek Harness).

**API keys are optional.** Enter them in `bookmark-research setup` (hidden input, checked immediately, saved in a private local file) or set environment variables, which take precedence.

| Variable | Service | Without it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EXA_API_KEY` | Exa search and page reading | Anonymous use where Exa allows it |
| `PARALLEL_API_KEY` | Parallel search and page reading | Free anonymous use with lower limits |
| `TAVILY_API_KEY` | Tavily search fallback and extraction | Keyless mode |
| `JINA_API_KEY` | Jina search | Jina Reader still reads pages anonymously |
| `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | Optional DeepSeek Search / Fetch | Not selected; other providers still work |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Optional OpenAI Deep Research runs | Feature off; host-led research still works |

Keys are never accepted in chat, command arguments or JSON files. Preferences can also be changed by asking the agent in a client session ("Show Bookmark Research settings", "Use only Exa for future searches"); it uses the `update_settings` tool.

## Where data is stored

Nothing is written into your bookmark files or the plugin. The data directory is `$BOOKMARK_RESEARCH_DATA_DIR`, or `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bookmark-research`.

| Location | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `research/` (or `<input>.bookmark-research/` beside the input) | One folder per research task: report, sources, evidence, and `work/` for the agent's intermediate files |
| `research-locations.json` | Where every task folder is, so tasks stay listed after the location setting changes |
| `knowledge/` | Saved page reads: `sources/` per fetch, `pages/` with each distinct text stored once |
| `wiki/` | Reviewed knowledge pages and revisions; `index.md` catalog and `log.md` timeline |
| `index.sqlite3`, `index.sqlite3.sources/` | Bookmark search index and managed snapshots of imported packages |
| `raw-library.sqlite3` | Rebuildable full-text index for `search_archive` |
| `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/bookmark-research/` | `settings.json` and `credentials.json` (private, owner-only) |

Changing the location affects new research only; existing tasks stay where they are.

## Research loops and delegation

The host model plans the research, searches or reads pages, evaluates the evidence and follows unresolved questions. The Skill guides this loop; MCP stores inputs, evidence, budgets and progress. Saving a research task does not start a background agent.

For a grouped report, the plugin supplies a reader → fresh verifier → coverage check → follow-up → report workflow. Codex uses its native subagent tools and the bundled delegation guide; Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness (dsh) use available host workflow hooks. The host owns concurrency, cancellation and agent lifetime. All children must receive the relevant instructions and access the same research store.

The workflow adapters have simulated contract tests, but a successful install does not prove that every host can execute the complete multi-agent workflow. See [host workflows](skills/bookmark-research/references/host-workflows.md) for requirements. Historical validation records are available in Git history.

## What's inside

A bundle of one Skill, one local MCP server, and the remote MCPs and services that server connects to. The client registers only the local MCP.

| Layer | Component | Runs as | Setup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Skill | [`bookmark-research`](skills/bookmark-research/SKILL.md) and method references, each with a [Chinese copy](skills/bookmark-research/references/zh/skill-guide.md) | Loaded by the client | None |
| Local MCP | `bookmark-research`, 21 default tools (below) | Python process started by the client | Installed for you |
| Remote MCPs, called by the local MCP | [Exa](https://exa.ai) (search, page reading), [Parallel](https://parallel.ai) (search, fallback reading), [Tavily](https://tavily.com) (search fallback) | HTTPS, no local process | Optional API keys |
| HTTP services, called by the local MCP | [Jina Reader](https://jina.ai/reader) (fallback reading; search with a key); [DeepSeek Search / Fetch](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/search/) (optional; raw JSON tools API) | HTTPS | Optional `JINA_API_KEY`, `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` |
| Optional client MCPs | Exa Agent, Parallel Task MCP, Tavily Research | Added to your client by you | `bookmark-research setup` shows the steps |

Default MCP tools:

| Group | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Canvas context | `sync_package`, `index_status`, `search_bookmarks`, `get_context`, `plan_research` |
| Web and archives | `search_web`, `fetch_web`, `search_archive` |
| Wiki | `wiki_write`, `wiki_get`, `wiki_list`, `wiki_search` |
| Research API | `research_services`, `research_service_prepare`, `_start`, `_status`, `_result`, `_cancel`, `_attach` |
| Settings | `get_settings`, `update_settings` |

`plan_research` retrieves local candidates and independently checks the Wiki/archive; the host assesses relevance and follows gaps. It also works without a Canvas source. `wiki_write` accepts authored sections, exact citations and source text or capture IDs in one call. Research APIs accept a question without a local research session.

The `deep` preset additionally exposes source maintenance, persistent research records, routing diagnostics and Wiki maintenance. These support explicit audits and resumption. Git history uses the host's shell.

Tool descriptions: [details](docs/details.en.md#mcp-tools).

## More

- [Installation guide](docs/installation.en.md): all install options, npm updates and source development
- [User guide](docs/user-guide.en.md): first use, the three research modes, languages
- [Details](docs/details.en.md): data model, research modes, settings, export formats, development checks
- [Architecture](docs/bookmark-research-architecture.md) (Chinese)

Originally developed in [Bookmark Canvas](https://github.com/Browser-bookmark-hub/Bookmark-Canvas). License: [GPL-3.0](LICENSE).

# DSH Keys Manager

[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-keys-manager)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-keys-manager)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E22.19%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24-339933)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-keys-manager)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-%5E0.2.1--rc.3-0969DA)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm)

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns one provider API key into a managed pool.
It extends the Models page rather than replacing it: providers, models, and the
model picker stay where they are; only the API-key source moves behind the
manager.

## What it does

**Pool and routing**

- Several keys per provider, each with an alias and a health state.
- One key pinned to a session, round-robin for new sessions; a failing request
  is retried on its key, then moved to another key.
- Exponential cooldown recovery, capped at seven days.

**Accounts and sign-in**

- Seven pi-ai OAuth providers can join the pool as an account instead of a
  pasted key.
- Two more sign in through the plugin's own bundled clients: Kilo and Z.AI
  Coding Plan.
- Seven companion transport routes for providers the vendored pi-ai cannot
  speak: Cursor, Devin, the two Google routes, Factory Droid, and the two
  GitLab Duo routes.

**Interface**

- A search-driven Keys Manager page on the plugin's own detail page.
- A "managed by Keys Manager" badge inside the existing Models provider cards.
- Extra built-in providers installed as ordinary `llm-pi-ai` routes — 35 of
  them, listed under [Provider coverage](#provider-coverage).

## Quick start

### Install

In the Desktop or Web app, open **Plugins → Add plugin**, enter `dsh-keys-manager`,
click **Install**, then **Enable now**. This installs the same published package
as the CLI path, already carrying its built bundle.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-keys-manager
```

One install yields both bundles, `dsh-keys-manager` and `llm-omp-transports`;
enable both — the manager owns credentials and routing, the transport the seven
routes' wire protocols. Refresh the Web page afterwards for the browser half.

<details>
<summary>Install from a local checkout</summary>

```sh
git clone https://github.com/btspoony/dsh-keys-manager
cd dsh-keys-manager
pnpm i
dsh plugin --profile web link .
```

`add` installs the published tarball with its built `lib/` and client bundle;
`link .` builds them via `prepare` during `pnpm i`, as does `prepack` when packing.

</details>

## Use it

### Take over a provider and add keys

1. Search for a provider. Open **Plugins → Keys Manager → View** (`Plugins →
   密钥管理 → 查看` in the Chinese locale); the manager renders on the plugin's
   detail page. Existing DSH providers appear first; the plugin also ships the
   curated extra catalog described under [Provider coverage](#provider-coverage).
2. Adopt a provider. For an existing provider the manager imports the
   currently resolved credential, writes a broker reference into the provider
   profile, and leaves the original key in the credential store so release can
   restore it.
3. Add more keys with an alias. Every key is stored in the Harness credential
   store under its own reference; the manager state document never contains a
   key literal.
4. Manage a key from the three-dot menu: rename, pause/resume, delete. A key
   row shows status, last use, and the recovery time while cooling.
5. Tune retry count (1–3), base cooldown, and recovery grace in the settings
   card.

### Accounts and sign-in

Providers that ship a native OAuth sign-in offer two ways to join the pool:
**Add key** stores a static API key, while **Add account** runs the provider's
OAuth sign-in flow and stores the result as an account row in the same pool.
Nine routes join as an **account**: seven through pi-ai's own flows, `kilo` and
`zai` through the plugin's bundled clients (device code, pasted `zcode://`
redirect), which mint a **static** credential renewed only by **Sign in again**.

| Route group | How it joins | Refresh / renew |
|---|---|---|
| 9 OAuth accounts | **Add account** — seven pi-ai flows, two plugin clients | provider-managed for the seven; **Sign in again** for the two static credentials |
| 7 transport routes | **Transport accounts** — one grant per route | see [Transport routes](#transport-routes) |

**API keys form the selection ring** — sticky sessions, round-robin, retry
failover and cooldowns operate across the provider's keys — while **one
projected OAuth grant serves its provider**, and an account row's counters
reflect only that account's own successes and failures. Per-account ranking is
future work. When the projected grant fails, the account cools down and the
pool falls back to its keys, or stops serving on an OAuth-only route until a
manual re-login.

**`muse-code` needs no transport or account row of its own**: the vendored pi-ai
`meta` route (`openai-responses` on `https://api.meta.ai/v1`) serves it, the
agreement check was static, and the first live call is a manual smoke check per
[Known limits](docs/known-limits.md).

### Transport routes

Providers the vendored pi-ai cannot speak are served by the companion
`dsh-llm-omp-transports` component:

- One grant per route, at `llm-omp-transports/<route>` — no key pool and no
  per-account rotation. Sign-in happens in the **Transport accounts** section of
  the Keys Manager page.
- Models are generated from the pinned `@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog@18.12.3` table when
  the transport is built, and the clients are unofficial: read the
  [transports package docs](packages/llm-omp/README.md) and its
  [known limits](packages/llm-omp/docs/known-limits.md) before relying on them.

| Route | Sign-in | Refresh | Model rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | browser page + poll | on the credential seam | 123 |
| `devin` | paste the landed callback URL | none — sign in again | 2 |
| `google-gemini-cli` | loopback `8085` + paste fallback | on the credential seam | 7 |
| `google-antigravity` | loopback `51121` + paste fallback | on the credential seam | 22 |
| `factory-droid` | WorkOS device code (URL + user code) | one refresh in a 60 s window, keeps `orgId`/`region` | 62 |
| `gitlab-duo` | PKCE loopback `localhost:8080/callback`, no port fallback, paste fallback | one refresh in a 60 s window | 16 |
| `gitlab-duo-agent` | paste the `vscode://` URL | one refresh, echoes the `vscode` redirect | 1 |

<details>
<summary>Per-route notes</summary>

- **Cursor** — streams text and reasoning and hands tool calls to DSH's tool
  loop; images are refused with a typed error. The client presents Cursor's
  vendor-internal OAuth identity.
- **Devin** — no refresh: a static bearer whose expiry is derived from the token
  (JWT `exp` minus five minutes, else one year), and without a readable expiry
  the row shows `active` with a blank countdown column.
- **Google routes** — both share one generated `lib/omp/google.mjs` artifact yet
  keep separate grants, account rows and catalogs. The grant is
  `{access, refresh, expires, projectId, email?}`; sign-in resolves the Cloud
  project the route bills, and a `legacy-tier` or paid account whose project
  cannot be discovered fails `AUTH_FAILED` until `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` (or
  `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID`) is set.
- **Factory Droid** — four wires behind one proxy, chosen by model id inside the
  artifact; rows carry no base URL and the account's residency
  (`orgId`/`region`) survives refresh.
- **GitLab Duo pair** — `gitlab-duo`'s direct-access token cache is keyed on the
  GitLab token, so a rotated token misses it; `gitlab-duo-agent` re-seeds a
  workflow per request and replays the transcript rather than resuming a socket.

</details>

### Selection and failure policy

| Mechanism | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Sticky session | The first request of a session selects a key and binds it for that session/provider pair. Later requests reuse it. |
| Round robin | A new session advances the provider cursor and takes the next healthy key. |
| Retry | A failing request is retried on the same key `retryCount` times. Request-shaped failures such as `CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED` and cancellation never cool a key. |
| Switch | After the retry budget is spent, the failing key is marked cooling, and the session is rebound to another healthy key. When no alternate key exists, the manager delegates to the composition's normal retry/fallback policy. |
| Cooldown | The first failure cools a key for `baseCooldownMs`. A failure while cooling, or within `recoveryGraceMs` after recovery, doubles the next cooldown; a long healthy gap resets the escalation. The hard cap is seven days. |
| Recovery | The key is automatically selectable again when its cooldown expires; no manual reset is required. |

## Configuration & data

Manager metadata lives at:

```text
$DSH_HOME/keys-manager/state.json
```

with owner-only permissions. It contains aliases, credential references,
health counters, session bindings, and provider adoption facts. API key
literals live only in the Harness credential store; an account row follows the
same rule behind its `grantRef`, with only non-sensitive metadata (email,
account id, expiry) in the state. The file is written atomically through a
temporary file and a rename.

Each managed provider profile points its `apiKeyEnv` at a broker reference
such as `KEYSMGR_ZAI_CODING_CN_3FA2C1`. The Host credential layer answers that
reference per request with the session's selected key. The Models page sees
the profile as configured; writing directly to the broker reference is
refused with a pointer to the manager.

<details>
<summary>OAuth2 extension point</summary>

The state shape already distinguishes `kind: "api-key"` from `kind: "oauth"`
and keeps a nullable `oauth` object beside the credential reference. A future
account flow can add records under `keys-manager/<provider>/<key>` without
rewriting existing rows. Providers whose only authentication is OAuth are
reported as unsupported in this version rather than being treated as API-key
providers.

</details>

## Provider coverage

Four groups, one pool:

- **DSH built-in** — routes from the shipped DSH pi-ai catalog. The set follows
  your installed DSH version, so the Models page is the authoritative list; four
  of them are outside single-key pooling (below).
- **Plugin extra built-in** — 35 routes this plugin adds as ordinary
  `llm-pi-ai` routes.
