# DSH Vibeify

**Turn your AI work into a living magazine.**

DSH Vibeify is an open-source, local magazine for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It gives AI work a visual, content-first home: use DeepSeek, ChatGPT, or both; keep Chat for control; and share only the finished article you choose.

Vibeify 0.17.1 improves magazine-card and image recovery while retaining **DeepSeek-led with OpenAI support**: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 leads through `deepseek-flash`, with GPT-6.1 Sol available for bounded tasks through ChatGPT-authenticated Codex. This mode uses Harness 0.2.1-rc.2 and Codex 0.164.0. See [the installation route](docs/INSTALL.md#deepseek-led-with-openai-support).

[![Watch the real DSH Vibeify welcome edition and finished walkthrough](docs/assets/dsh-vibeify-magazine-social.png)](https://youtu.be/jda4uplWsiI)

[Release 0.17.1](https://github.com/N9-Developer-Empowerment/DSH-Vibeify/releases/tag/v0.17.1) · [Source tag](https://github.com/N9-Developer-Empowerment/DSH-Vibeify/tree/v0.17.1) · [Download release assets](https://github.com/N9-Developer-Empowerment/DSH-Vibeify/releases/tag/v0.17.1) · [Watch the finished walkthrough](https://youtu.be/jda4uplWsiI) · [See how it works](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md) · [Get installation help](docs/FAQ.md) · [Email Vibeify](mailto:info@codingforjustice.org.uk)

The real 2:24 demonstration opens Vibe with content, turns a Chat request into a visual card, uses an explicit Update, then previews one article privately before optional publication. [Watch it on YouTube.](https://youtu.be/jda4uplWsiI)

DSH Vibeify's magazine is **not** a public website. It turns [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)—a local runtime for agents, models, tools, permissions and sessions—into a creator-first streaming experience that *behaves* like a website. Vibe is the visual, content-first home; Chat remains underneath for detailed requests, progress, approvals, Queue, Steer and technical evidence. An optional, deliberately separate share service can publish one reviewed article at a time without exposing the local magazine or requiring the recipient to have DSH, ChatGPT, or DeepSeek.

## The idea: generative AI beyond turn-by-turn chat

Most AI products begin with an empty box. The person writes a prompt, waits for one answer, and repeats. DSH Vibeify begins with something useful to explore and turns Chat work from any thread into one continuous edition. Returning readers open their saved edition, newest stories first. A configured editorial direction takes precedence over the local welcome issue. First-time readers without a direction can still explore local orientation pages without a model call; **Update my magazine** or **Update VIBE now** requests a fresh people-centred issue. **Look & feel** controls the magazine palette, text size and spacing separately from Chat. For an explicit public-content request, each complete verified card can arrive while the rest of the answer is still being made; ordinary final answers join after completion. It generates extra magazine material only when the reader asks for an update.

> **The one sentence to remember:** open Chat and say **“Make a Vibe about…”** when you want a deliberately edited Vibe article or series. That explicit wording tells the active DSH lead to use Vibeify's visual, linked, complete-chunk publishing contract. An ordinary Chat answer may still join Vibe after it finishes, but it is not guaranteed to receive the richer article structure or to stream card by card while the turn is running.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    OPEN["Open local DSH"] --> WELCOME["Evergreen welcome issue\nwhy · how · try it in Chat"]
    WELCOME --> VIBE["Vibe already contains a visual edition"]
    VIBE --> EXPLORE["Read · watch · save · respond"]
    RADAR["Shared public radar\ntrends · culture · technology"] --> CACHE["Local hidden reserve\nsignals · candidates · ready pages"]
    CACHE --> VIBE
    EXPLORE --> SIGNAL["A Chat request, pull-to-update, or Update click"]
    SIGNAL --> HARNESS["DSH harness\nsessions · tools · models · permissions"]
    HARNESS --> LEAD["Active lead agent\nplans and defines acceptance"]
    LEAD --> INSTANT["Local reserve\nready pages + visual short"]
    LEAD --> WORK["Independent specialist lanes\nquick · culture · media · deep"]
    WORK --> CHECK["Lead verifies each finished lane independently"]
    CHECK --> STREAM["Each closed editorial chunk streams immediately"]
    INSTANT --> VIBE
    STREAM --> VIBE
    STREAM --> STOP["One bounded update completes, then stops"]
    VIBE --> PREVIEW["Share one article\nprivate preview first"]
    PREVIEW -->|"reader presses Publish"| PUBLIC["Public article link\nno DSH account required"]
    EXPLORE -. "open when you want control or detail" .-> CHAT["Chat\nask · queue · steer · approve · inspect"]
    CHAT --> HARNESS
```

The visible surface is website-like, but the machinery underneath is an agent harness:

| Layer | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **DSH** | Runs sessions, agents, model routes, tools, permissions and approvals on the user's machine. |
| **Vibeify** | Adds the continuous editorial stream, visual presentation, local content buffer and safe route between generated work and the stream. |
| **Vibe** | Presents every thread's completed answers—and complete verified cards from an active public-content request—as one newest-first edition. A hidden local reserve may be prepared while Vibe is in recent use; only Pull to update, Update, a closed public-content card, or a completed Chat answer changes the visible magazine. It is not a separate public site. |
| **Chat** | Lets the user ask directly, queue or steer work, approve protected actions and inspect progress or technical evidence. |
| **Lead agent** | Plans, sets the acceptance bar, validates work and owns the final result. This is Codex in ChatGPT-only mode, or native DeepSeek in DeepSeek-only and DeepSeek-led/OpenAI-support modes. |
| **Workers** | Optionally perform bounded research, coding, analysis or media work; their output is not published merely because they say it is finished. |
| **Optional share service** | Receives one allow-listed, reader-reviewed article only after **Share** is clicked, shows a private preview, and performs a public write only after a second **Publish public link** click. It never receives the Chat prompt, reasoning, session identity, settings, local history, or credentials. |

“Streaming” here means a continuous stream of **complete, formatted content items**, not merely text appearing token by token. The edition is available immediately from local bundled, saved, and ready-reserve material. A deliberate pull or Update click releases ready pages immediately, including a visual short, then uses one foreground batch only when the reserve is short. During an explicit public-content Chat request, the first short verified card arrives before the whole series is researched and each later closed card follows independently; ordinary un-enveloped final answers join after durable completion. Neither route makes an extra AI call. Opening, scrolling, changing settings, or finishing a batch never changes the visible edition by itself.

This is the different paradigm: **Chat is an available control surface, not the whole product.** Each Chat thread remains request-driven and becomes idle after it answers. Vibe is the shared presentation layer across those threads, with an explicit update gesture when the reader wants more.

For a plain-English walkthrough of the two surfaces, instant local reserve, parallel agent lanes, complete-page streaming, stop conditions, provider modes, and privacy boundary, read [How DSH Vibeify works](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md).

Choose the provider setup that suits you:

- **DeepSeek only:** native DSH/DeepSeek runs the agent and the provider-neutral Vibe package supplies the experience.
- **ChatGPT only:** a ChatGPT-authenticated Codex agent leads and works without an OpenAI API key.
- **Both (DeepSeek leads, OpenAI supports):** native DeepSeek plans and owns the final answer; an optional GPT-6.1 Sol Codex worker can handle bounded subtasks through ChatGPT sign-in. The lead reviews the worker's result.

The original Codex-led mode remains available as **ChatGPT only** (`--provider chatgpt` for the developer installer). For the new **Both** mode, connect DeepSeek under DSH **Settings → Models** and sign in to Codex with ChatGPT if you want the optional worker. Installation can finish before either account is connected. DeepSeek billing and ChatGPT plan limits remain separate.

The first screen is Vibe itself: a full-screen editorial feed opens with the current welcome issue, followed by a bundled content well and the reader's older saved magazine. No guide, tile, recipe, or prompt must be selected. The welcome issue repeatedly points to one useful next move: open **Chat**, say **“Make a Vibe about…”**, watch the completed visual pages enter Vibe, then preview and share a good one. A new answer made during the current visit arrives above the welcome issue. Older saved pages remain further down rather than being deleted or mistaken for today's front page. **Chat** remains the detailed source view with the conventional DSH conversation and technical controls.

> DSH is a fast-moving developer preview. Vibeify pins the versions it has tested and includes a health check, but you should still expect upstream changes.

## Play inside the article

Ask Chat to **“Make a Vibe with an embedded game, calculator, form or interactive graph.”** Self-contained interactive panels appear within the article. Open a panel to use it while reading; the built-in Mochi Meadow game is visible immediately and starts only when you press its start button.

The article carries the interaction into its private sharing preview and published page when the matching share-service version is deployed. Mochi Meadow uses the same implementation in all three places. Scores and form answers stay in the open panel; they are not saved or included in the shared article. Closing a panel or reloading resets its state. Panels cannot access your magazine, account, external services or local files.

Shared articles keep prose in a readable column while games and interactive panels use the available article width. Lead images preserve their aspect ratio in a bounded, centered frame, and supported media players appear in both preview and publication. One stylesheet and shared sizing and media policies govern both sharing views.

See [interactive article authoring](docs/VIBES.md#embedded-games-and-interactive-articles) and [sharing](docs/SHARING.md). Updating local Vibeify does not deploy the separate public share service.

## Contact

For Vibeify questions, installation help, or responsible reports that should not begin in a public issue, email [info@codingforjustice.org.uk](mailto:info@codingforjustice.org.uk). Do not send passwords, API keys, cookies, OAuth tokens, private prompts, session exports, or unreviewed logs.

## Start here

### I am curious, but not a developer

Think of DSH as a control room for AI agents. DSH Vibeify changes that control room in three important ways:

1. **The product starts with content, not a task form.** Read, scroll, save, watch, listen, or answer an optional question; open Chat only when you want to make or solve something.
2. **Every tile is visual.** A stable locally bundled photograph is available without a model or network wait. Generated magazine pages seek subject-relevant public imagery; if a catalogue photo fails to load, a labelled conceptual illustration is used. Long features can carry several photographic beats, and AI-assisted graphics remain explicitly labelled.
3. **Provider choice is clear.** Choose DeepSeek only, ChatGPT only, or DeepSeek-led work with optional OpenAI support. The lead model is stated for each route.

It does not switch provider mode without telling you, send your images elsewhere, approve emails or other external actions for you, or promise equivalent quality where no Codex verification step is present.

### I want to try it

For the verified Apple-silicon macOS route, [download the installer](https://dsh-vibeify.ezzye.chatgpt.site/DSH-Vibeify-Installer-macOS.zip), unzip it, and open **Install DSH Vibeify.command**. It installs or updates DSH and Vibeify, lets you choose DeepSeek only, ChatGPT only, DeepSeek with OpenAI support, or later, runs checks, and opens DSH. It never asks for an API key.

The repository also contains friendly **Windows** and **Linux** preview installers. They use the same public-source, immutable-package, provider-choice, non-billing-check, and do-not-interrupt-active-work contract. They will remain visibly labelled preview until the complete path has passed on real Windows and representative Linux machines; a Mac-only test is not treated as cross-platform evidence. See [Installation](docs/INSTALL.md) for the current downloads and [Installation and help FAQ](docs/FAQ.md) for check-only mode and private, free-chat troubleshooting.

For the developer route you need Node.js 22.19+ in the 22.x line, or Node.js 24+, and Git:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/N9-Developer-Empowerment/DSH-Vibeify.git
cd DSH-Vibeify
./scripts/install-dsh.sh --replace
./scripts/install-vibeify.sh --provider deepseek-codex # DeepSeek leads, optional GPT-6.1 Sol worker
# Or choose deepseek (DeepSeek only), chatgpt (Codex leads), or auto (preserve/detect mode)
./scripts/doctor.sh
dsh web
```

The installer does not restart a DSH process that is already running. Finish active work first. If DSH is already open on port 3080, reuse that page instead of starting a second copy.

For screenshots, alternative profiles, DeepSeek credentials, updating, migration, and removal, read the [full installation guide](docs/INSTALL.md). For the product lifecycle before or after installation, see [How it works](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md).

## What you get

- **A continuous, website-like local magazine.** Vibe covers the DSH work surface completely and opens directly into one long, responsive edition. There is no catalogue-to-player-to-result transition.
- **A welcome issue that sells the choice again.** Twenty-one visual, reader-facing panels explain the benefits and everyday use of Vibe, Chat, deliberate updates, editorial direction, local learning, imagery, saving, sharing, Queue/Steer, Think/Trajectory, connected apps, DSH, plugins, open source, provider and capability choices, permissions and safe updates. Each panel offers a concrete prompt and a direct route into Chat. The issue is rebuilt from the active plugin rather than cached, so an upgrade cannot reopen with last version's onboarding.
- **A deep, findable local well.** Twenty-four deterministic editorial chunks—text, credited photography and AI-assisted graphics—are available synchronously on a cold visit. Every tile receives one of twelve bundled visuals with varied crop and treatment, later images decode lazily, and up to 160 completed magazine items persist for 30 days. **Find Vibes** searches their titles and article text locally; 96 places inside the same total are protected for completed Chat-made Vibes so editorial refills cannot crowd all of them out.
- **Instant, bounded updates.** Pull down from the top of Vibe—including a two-finger pull on a Mac trackpad—or choose **Update**. Ready pages are released from the hidden reserve synchronously; a local visual short ensures an immediate response even when the reserve is empty. If fewer than four ready pages exist, one bounded foreground batch fills the gap and streams complete pages independently. **Stop update** cancels only that dedicated foreground turn, and a 20-minute ceiling stops a stuck update.
- **A shared radar, private editing.** A transparent GitHub Action publishes a public, content-only trend catalogue every 30 minutes. It contains headlines, links, regions and broad tribe hints—never reader history. Each installation keeps its selected tribes, free-text editor note, interactions, candidates, ready pages and spending ledger in that browser.
- **A deliberately overstocked reserve.** While the browser is open, Vibe was used within 24 hours, background editing is enabled, and the local ready reserve is below target, a separate hidden editor may prepare 6–8 pages. Codex-led mode uses bounded DeepSeek execution with Codex review; native DeepSeek modes keep their distinct no-Codex-verification boundary. The conservative reservation ledger hard-stops at the chosen daily maximum, never above **US $2**.
- **Newest-first, append-only depth.** Fresh chunks join the top of the same edition while storage remains append-only. They never replace earlier material; deeper research becomes a visible editorial follow-up above the earlier page.
- **Direction belongs in settings and Chat.** Automatic preference-questionnaire cards are removed, including legacy cards. Change the mix through VIBE settings or an explicit request. Saves, opens, plays and deliberate skips still inform the local editor; its learning stays on-device and has a one-click reset.
- **One magazine across every real Chat thread.** Vibe passively follows ordinary reader sessions for complete verified `chat-` cards, then reads durable DSH history as the fallback and for un-enveloped final answers. It never reopens or resumes a thread. Internal subagents, the dedicated foreground update and the hidden background editor are never mistaken for reader conversations. Transport envelopes are removed during cache migration; card titles are not repeated in their bodies, and Markdown tables remain structured. Raw prompts, half-written envelopes, worker reports, candidate lists, attachments, reasoning, tool activity, approvals, session identifiers, aborted work and incomplete progress are never copied.
- **No empty wait or hidden work.** Bundled and saved content render in the first local frame. A content-free ledger measures first frame, restore, explicit updates, chunk arrival, and engagement. Simply reading the magazine consumes no model quota.
- **Real photography, labelled generated visuals, and unique public covers.** Six locally bundled photographs and six labelled local AI-assisted SVG compositions provide a zero-wait private fallback; they are not the live editorial catalogue. Generated pages seek verified subject-relevant public imagery; long features may show separately credited photographs. A failed catalogue photo falls back to a labelled conceptual illustration. Each batch considers at least 18 potential images from three or more credible source families, ranks exact subject/entity relevance, informative value, credit clarity, composition, freshness and recent-use diversity, and publishes only the best choices. If exact photography is unavailable, an authorised story-specific generated image is preferred to recycled stock; a unique graphic or typographic treatment is the labelled fallback. The browser accepts reviewed catalogue hosts or a direct first-party image paired with a separate official page on the exact same HTTPS host; arbitrary third-party images stay blocked. It remembers 80 recently used remote image URLs, suppresses referrer data, removes rejected image syntax from article prose, and falls back locally if a remote image fails. Public sharing preserves the selected lead image and its credits through preview, publication and social previews. Typographic fallback covers use one shared design locally and in the public JPEG. Saved local cards—including their visual provenance—age out with the bounded 30-day/160-item magazine cache.
- **Optional image-source plugin.** The separate `dsh-visuals` package is auto-discovered and keeps Vibeify usable when absent. Wikimedia Commons and Openverse work without keys. A standalone image credit linking to a Commons File page is also resolved to its verified image, including credits with the author outside the link; optional Pexels and Pixabay keys are entered under **Settings → Images** and stay in DSH's write-only credential store. Only a short explicit-magazine title is searched—never ordinary Chat copy, prompts, attachments, history or settings—and every accepted result keeps its creator, licence and original source.
- **Useful exits from every panel.** Visual credits stay attached to their images. Every generated panel carries a separate, relevant content destination in the article copy—for example the story, original work, official creator page, paper, video, music or useful service—and Vibe repeats that destination as a compact **Read source** action. Image files and visual-credit pages are never presented as the article link.
- **Review before sharing.** Every finished card has **Preview and share**. It opens the fixed first-party share origin, waits for an exact-origin handshake, and transfers only that card's title, rendered Markdown, selected public images, credits, source link, kind, publication time and appearance enum and—when present—one allow-listed YouTube, Vimeo, Spotify or SoundCloud destination. The preview cannot publish automatically: the reader must inspect it and choose **Publish public link**. A separately deployed public service is required before publication is available. See [Sharing one Vibe article](docs/SHARING.md).
- **Simple manual link sharing.** Copy an existing public link or use your device’s share action, then make the final post yourself. Private Vibe articles retain their separate preview and explicit **Publish public link** step. No social account setup, scheduling or automatic posting. See [Sharing](docs/SHARING.md).
- **Provider-neutral Vibe.** `dsh-vibeify-experience` supplies Vibe without installing a Codex provider, so native DSH/DeepSeek remains in control.
- **Optional governed mode.** `dsh-vibeify` uses ChatGPT-authenticated Codex and deliberately removes OpenAI API-key fallbacks from the child process. In this mode Codex remains the lead.
- **DeepSeek-led OpenAI support.** `dsh-vibeify-deepseek` keeps native DeepSeek as the lead and adds a separate Vibeify preset with an optional one-shot GPT-6.1 Sol worker. DeepSeek reviews the returned evidence and owns the final answer. The original Standard preset remains available.
- **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 lead.** The Vibeify DeepSeek preset uses the official `deepseek-flash` alias as its main route. Its optional GPT-6.1 Sol worker is available for bounded tasks through ChatGPT sign-in.
- **A route-specific quality gate.** In Codex-led mode, Codex sets acceptance criteria and checks returned DeepSeek evidence. In DeepSeek-led mode, the DeepSeek lead reviews optional Codex-worker results before deciding what to use. A worker's own claim of success is not the acceptance check.
- **Choose your Codex lead.** In ChatGPT-only mode, open **Settings → Codex** to choose the signed-in main model and supported thinking effort. This setting does not change the DeepSeek-led route's GPT-6.1 Sol specialist, which is fixed for that worker.
- **A safe update centre.** Open **Settings → Updates** to check the installed DSH, Vibeify, and bundled Codex agent separately. A newer Codex release is not labelled installable until Vibeify has qualified it. The updater route is platform-aware: macOS opens the verified friendly updater, while Windows and Linux open their clearly labelled preview/help route until real-machine qualification is complete.
- **Clearer live work.** Chat receives useful progress, Queue or Steer controls remain available while the agent is busy, and explicit magazine updates or public-content requests can publish closed, source-checked chunks into Vibe without exposing reasoning or raw worker prose. Vibeify opens the current Think disclosure while work is live, then closes that same disclosure once when the final answer settles; the reader can reopen it without the interface fighting back.
- **Fewer unnecessary prompts.** Local work follows the selected DSH/Codex permissions; protected external actions still require the applicable confirmation route.
- **Connected apps.** In Codex-led mode, installed tools use their normal Codex approval boundaries. The native Codex worker cannot complete protected connected-app requests or ask a person questions; those requests fail closed and return to the lead.
- **Image support.** Images can be uploaded to Codex; sending them to another provider always requires explicit intent.
- **Colour and editorial settings.** In Chat, **VIBE settings** combines colour themes with any mix of 15 broad audience lenses—from Global & curious, Gen Z and Builders & nerds to Culture & arts, parents, sport and local life. It also controls useful surprise, a free-text editor note, background reserve filling, gentle content notes and a clearly denominated **USD/day** DeepSeek maximum. Colour remains presentation-only; editorial settings never change permissions or protected-action approval.

## How bounded workers are reviewed

No route promises lower total cost or identical results on every task. DeepSeek API use and ChatGPT plan use are separate. A worker can add value when a task is bounded, but the lead still has to review its evidence and decide whether to use it.

The Codex-led route may send well-defined execution packets to a DeepSeek worker when:

- the task is self-contained;
- its result can be checked independently;
- the selected model has the right capability; and
- the same acceptance bar can be maintained.

Codex does not simply ask whether the worker says it succeeded. It inspects the actual diff, files, test results, sources, or other task evidence. Passing work is reused; Codex repairs only failed or unverifiable parts instead of pointlessly repeating everything.

In the DeepSeek-led route, DeepSeek chooses whether a bounded task is suitable for the optional GPT-6.1 Sol worker. The worker uses a workspace-write sandbox with Codex automatic permission review. The lead reviews its result; it does not transfer final acceptance to the worker. The two-worker limit is prompt policy, not a hard runtime cap.

Pricing and model availability change. Consult current provider information before estimating costs.

## Experience Shell and VIBEs

The **Vibe home** owns one lean-back magazine, the evergreen welcome issue, saved chunks, completed-Chat projections from every local thread, live complete cards from explicit public-content requests, update controls, and reading position. It is the landing page on every visit; a previous Chat visit is not restored as home. **Chat** reveals the normal DSH conversation, **Trajectory** retains technical work, and **Vibe** returns to the top. On launch the authored welcome issue appears before older saved material; any new page made during that visit is appended normally and rises above it. Completed answers and explicitly published chunks are retained in a bounded 30-day browser-local cache, while deterministic welcome and example pages are rebuilt from the installed plugin and never persisted. Prompts, session ids and working activity are not cached. The uppercase **VIBE settings** control remains separate: colour affects Chat presentation, while editorial direction affects only the next requested magazine update. Neither changes models, permissions, routing, protected-action confirmation, or billing policy. In DeepSeek-only mode, Codex-specific capability and progress controls are omitted. See [Vibe generated-content streaming](docs/CONTENT_STREAMING.md) for the lifecycle, live semantic-card route, local-history fallback, cache, timing, chunking, and worker method.

Select **Chat**, then **VIBE settings** at the bottom-right of the conventional DSH UI to choose a colour palette, a broad editorial direction, and an optional free-text editor note. These settings are stored only in that browser; the direction is passed to the lead only when you next pull to update or choose **Update**. Select the visually highlighted **Vibe · Magazine** session tab to return directly to the newest material.

Daniela Elliott leads the project’s experience design, look and feel, and visual VIBEs. The current palettes are a starting point for a more expressive, user-shaped agent workspace. See [VIBEs](docs/VIBES.md) to add or refine a palette.

## For developers

DSH Vibeify is both a real DSH bundle and a Codex helper plugin:

```text
DSH-Vibeify/
├── .agents/plugins/marketplace.json   # repository Codex marketplace
├── docs/                              # installation, design and security
├── plugins/dsh-vibeify/
│   ├── .codex-plugin/plugin.json      # Codex plugin manifest
│   ├── cordis.patch.yml               # DSH bundle configuration
│   ├── index.js                       # Codex adapter and worker routing
│   ├── codex-capability.js            # lead capability presets
│   ├── codex-settings.js              # live DSH settings integration
│   ├── delegation-contract.js         # worker/acceptance boundary
│   ├── progressive-output.js          # live final-answer delta bridge
│   ├── update-check.js                # fixed-source version and compatibility checks
│   ├── client-src/experience/         # stream shell, playout, cache, timing and catalogue modules
│   ├── preview/                       # isolated visual iteration harness
│   ├── client.js                      # generated DSH browser artifact
│   └── skills/dsh-vibeify/SKILL.md    # Codex operational guidance
├── plugins/dsh-vibeify-experience/    # provider-neutral DSH client package
├── plugins/dsh-visuals/               # optional public-image search and secure key references
├── plugins/dsh-social-desk/           # optional reviewed local social queue and official API adapters
├── services/vibe-share/               # optional account-free public article host
├── shared/vibe-share-contract.js      # allow-list boundary shared by DSH and host
└── scripts/                            # macOS, Windows and Li

# dsh-plugin-speech

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

![Read aloud — DeepSeek Harness speech plugin](docs/cover.jpg)

Read assistant replies aloud in [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), one continuous voice per reply.

## What it does

Each finished assistant message gets a play control in its action row. Press it and the reply is spoken through a text-to-speech service; press it again and it stops. A settings row in General owns the service, the voice, and the tuning.

The whole reply goes out in **one request** and the host streams the audio back while the service is still synthesizing it. The browser holds back only the first **1.5 seconds** of audio — enough to cover the first chunk's jitter — and starts the voice: measured at about **one second** from the click, with a two-minute reading arriving in under two seconds from then on.

## Providers

| Service | Key needed | Voices |
|---|---|---|
| **Microsoft Edge** (default) | no | the service publishes its full catalog, every language it serves |

Adding a provider means adding one folder under `src/providers/` and one line in `src/providers/registry.ts` — the settings screen builds its fields from what the provider declares.

### The Edge token

Every handshake carries a short-lived `Sec-MS-GEC` token: the current time in Windows file-time ticks, rounded down to five minutes, digested together with the well-known client token. In October 2026 the endpoint moved to a **second generation** of that token — a patched SHA-256 paired with a 64-bit checksum — and began answering the first generation with a bare `403` (`Edge TTS WebSocket error: Unexpected server response: 403`), which is what a reply that never speaks looks like from the browser. `src/providers/edge/gec.ts` reproduces the accepted generation; `server.ts` hands it to `msedge-tts` by replacing the library's private URL builder, which is also what pins the token version the endpoint now expects. If read-aloud stops working again, test that token first: it is the only part of this plugin that can expire without the code changing.

## Requirements

- A DeepSeek Harness surface — `dsh web`, or the desktop app — version `0.2.0-rc.2` or newer.
- Network access to the speech service. Nothing else: there is no model to download, and the Edge provider needs no account.

The version floor is not decorative. The plugin's preferences are its own Cordis entry config, exposed to the settings screen as a form through `ctx.configForms`. Releases before `0.2.0-rc.2` had plugins register settings namespaces themselves (`settings.register`) and handed the browser a `ctx.settingsScope`; both services are gone.

## Install

This package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so it installs as a **profile bundle**: the package
manager links it, the launcher appends it to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, and the
bundle's own patch layer inserts the plugin row. Installing also enables it — in DeepSeek
Harness, installing a plugin and enabling it in a profile are separate steps, and a bundle
collapses the two.

**Desktop app** — sidebar → **Plugins** → **Add plugin**, then give one of:

- `@nakamuraia/dsh-plugin-speech` (the npm registry)
- `github:NakamuraIA/dsh-plugin-speech`
- an absolute path to a local checkout

**From the CLI** — the same operation, profile-scoped:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:NakamuraIA/dsh-plugin-speech
```

Restart the surface afterwards. The host half claims its HTTP routes when the plugin loads,
a desktop profile is owned by the app, and a newly installed out-of-tree bundle is not mounted
by a live recomposition — an app-internal row added to a patch does reload immediately, a
package that has to come from the profile's `node_modules` does not.

### One-off overlay, without installing

`cordis.patch.yml` is the same patch the bundle applies, so it also works as a temporary
command-line overlay:

```sh
dsh web --patch ./cordis.patch.yml
```

Do **not** do both. A profile patch that inserts `ui-speech` while the bundle is selected
collides with `duplicate loader entry id`; the profile layer is for overriding the row's
config, which is what the settings screen writes.

The **row name** is the package name and also the browser module id the built bundle registers
under; the **row id** (`ui-speech`) is the settings namespace the config form is keyed by.
Nothing works if either one drifts, so change the two together.

## Settings

Settings opens on **General**, where a **Read aloud** row owns:

- **Service** — which provider speaks.
- **Language** and **Voice** — the catalog entry to use.
- **Speed**, **Volume**, **Pitch** — sent to the service with every request.
- **Skip code** — leave fenced code and inline code out of the reading.
- **Test voice** — speaks a sample through the settings on screen, saved or not.

The row edits the plugin's own entry config, so the chosen values persist in the profile patch beside the entry rather than in a settings document. Resetting a field restores the schema default, and a write the Host refuses leaves the stored value untouched while the row says so.

Tables and pasted spreadsheets are never read, whichever way **Skip code** is set. That switch decides only whether fenced and inline code are read: with it off, the code itself is spoken and just the fences go. Links keep their label and lose their target; emoji, quotes, and standalone symbols are dropped. Sentence punctuation is kept, because the voice uses it for pauses.

## How it works

```
browser                    host                        service
───────                    ────                        ───────
click ─ ▶ POST /speech/speak { text }
                           select provider from
                           its own entry config
                           ────────────────────────── ▶ synthesize
        ◀ ─ audio bytes stream back ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ┘
play from the first 1.5 s, keep appending behind it
```

Synthesis lives on the host because a browser cannot hold an API key and cannot reach most services across CORS. The browser only posts text and plays bytes. Every editable leaf of the entry config is `.volatile()`, so a settings write lands in the running host without reloading it — the host reads the same value the browser wrote.

One request is the point. Every extra request pays a fresh handshake — around 0.9 s to the service — and adds a connection that can be dropped; sending the whole reply once means one handshake and one stream. The service is fast enough for that to be the right trade: measured at **73x realtime** on a warm connection and 1.5x on a cold one, so a two-minute reading arrives in under two seconds while the first second of it is already playing.

The 1.5-second head is the whole latency budget. It exists to cover the jitter between the first chunk and the next one, not to wait for a useful part of the reply: a smaller head starts playing on the first frame and occasionally stutters, a larger one buys nothing. If the stream dies after the voice started, what is already buffered still plays out; if the engine refuses the buffer outright the reply is played as one whole file instead.

A voice can also end every sentence with a long silence of its own — `pt-BR-AntonioNeural`, the schema default, leaves about 0.9 s at each one, while the multilingual voices leave none. That silence is in the audio the service returns, not in how this plugin plays it.

## Development

This repository builds on its own against the published `@deepseek-ai/*` packages; no harness checkout is involved:

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm build      # tsc → lib/types, tsdown → lib/index.js + lib/client.js
pnpm test       # vitest
pnpm typecheck  # sources and specs
```

`build/plugin-bundle.ts` is the client-bundle preset. It emits the `window.__ModuleLoader__.load` handoff, keeps every module-table row a `require`, compiles CSS Modules into one injected style tag, and fails the build on a cross-plugin value import. It is a self-contained copy of the harness preset, which is what lets the package be built here.

Three specs under `tests/checkout/` compose the real client registries, which only exist as sources inside a harness checkout; `tests/checkout/README.md` explains why and how to run them. Everything else, including the client wiring, runs through `pnpm test`.

### Migrating from 0.1.x

- The host half exports `Config` — the schemastery schema with `.volatile()` leaves — and no longer calls `settings.register`; the synthesis route reads the entry config it was handed at apply time.
- The client half takes `ctx.configForms.get('ui-speech')` instead of `ctx.settingsScope.bind(...)`, and a write reports acceptance directly (`Promise<boolean>`) instead of being checked against the settled section.

# 工具栏按钮（可选）

把「跑一遍验证」变成输入框旁边的一个盾牌按钮。**只适用于 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）**，
其他 MCP 客户端用不到它 —— 它们只有三个工具，没有输入框工具栏。

## 它做什么

| 动作 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 单击 | 把「快速检查」请求填进输入框（`fast=true`） |
| Shift + 单击 | 填「完整检查」请求（含测试与浏览器层） |
| 双击 | 撤销，恢复点击前的草稿 |

**它不会自动发送**：只把一段话写进输入框，你改完按回车才真的跑。
Client 侧拿不到 agent 的工具执行权，真正跑验证的是 Host 上的 MCP 工具。

双击撤销有一道保险：如果输入框里的内容已经被你改过，它会**拒绝撤销**并提示
「输入框已改动，未撤销」—— 宁可撤销失败，也不能把你打的字冲掉。

## 安装（DSH）

让 agent 装（推荐）：

```
用 plugin_manager 安装 plugin 目录：
target = /绝对路径/verify-helper/plugin
```

或者手动：把 `plugin/` 放进 DSH 的 profile，并在 `cordis.patch.yml` 里加

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: verify-helper-button
      name: '@local/verify-helper-button'
```

装完**刷新页面**，输入框左下角出现盾牌图标。

## 卸载

删掉上面那条 `insert` 即可，或让 agent 执行 `plugin_manager remove_bundle`。

## 自己改

`client.js` 是可读源码，改完刷新页面生效。里面两段提示词就是它填进输入框的内容：

```js
const PROMPT_FAST = '用验证助手检查当前项目（MCP 工具 verify_start，…fast=true）…'
const PROMPT_FULL = '用验证助手完整检查当前项目（…不加 fast）…'
```

想让它填别的要求（比如「顺便把结果写成 md」），改这两行就行。

# 验证助手 · verify-helper

[![CI](https://github.com/ngwddd/verify-helper/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ngwddd/verify-helper/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11%2B-3776ab.svg)](https://www.python.org/)

给**任意项目目录**跑一遍机械检查，返回 **PASS / FAIL / UNKNOWN** 三态结论，
每条结论都带证据（命令、退出码、`文件:行号`）、**风险等级**和**修复建议**。

既是一个命令行工具，也是一个 MCP 服务器（agent 可以直接调用）。

---

## 为什么做这个

Agent 的自验经常很水：跑个构建看到「成功」就宣称完成，但页面点了没反应、链接 404、
测试里根本没断言。有研究统计过 20,574 个真实编码会话，**22.58% 的失败来自「把没验证的状态说成已完成」**。

这个工具把「完成」的判定从模型的自我叙述里拿出来，交给可复核的输出：

- **没有 oracle（判定标准）的检查，一律记 UNKNOWN，绝不当 PASS。**
- **每条 FAIL 都附证据**：跑了什么命令、退出码多少、哪一行出问题。
- **每条 FAIL 都附修复建议**，不是只告诉你错了。

## 快速开始

```bash
# 直接跑（零依赖，Python 3.11+）
python verify_core.py /path/to/project

# 列出全部检查项
python verify_core.py --list-checks

# 快速模式：只跳过「测试」与「变异」（运行时和浏览器照跑）
python verify_core.py /path/to/project --fast

# 输出 SARIF（给 GitHub Code Scanning 用）
python verify_core.py /path/to/project --sarif out.sarif
```

退出码：`0 = PASS`，`1 = FAIL / UNKNOWN / 参数错误`。

### 作为 MCP 服务器

零依赖、纯 stdio，**只要 Python 3.11+，不用装任何包**：

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ngwddd/verify-helper.git
cd verify-helper
python server.py          # 前台起一个 stdio 服务器（客户端会自己拉起，一般不用手跑）
```

> macOS / Linux 上多半叫 `python3`，Windows 上叫 `python`。填配置时用**绝对路径**最稳。

#### 通用客户端配置（Claude Desktop / Cursor / VS Code / Windsurf 等）

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "verify-helper": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["/绝对路径/verify-helper/server.py"],
      "env": { "PYTHONIOENCODING": "utf-8" }
    }
  }
}
```

Windows 示例：

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "verify-helper": {
      "command": "C:\\Program Files\\Python314\\python.exe",
      "args": ["C:\\Users\\you\\verify-helper\\server.py"],
      "env": { "PYTHONIOENCODING": "utf-8" }
    }
  }
}
```

#### DeepSeek Harness（DSH）配置

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: verify-helper
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: verify-helper
        transport: stdio
        command: 'python'
        args: ['/绝对路径/verify-helper/server.py']
        env:
          PYTHONIOENCODING: utf-8
        toolCallTimeoutMs: 600000
        failOnStartupError: false
```

#### 装好了怎么确认

```bash
python verify_core.py --list-checks     # 应列出 16 项检查
```

客户端里应该出现三个工具：

| 工具 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `verify_start(path, checks?, fast?, format?)` | 跑一遍验证，`format` 可选 `text` / `json` / `sarif` |
| `verify_report(run_id?)` | 取回完整报告，默认最近一次 |
| `verify_checks()` | 列出全部检查项、风险等级、修复建议 |

FAIL 时返回 `isError: true` —— 调用方不会被「静默通过」骗过去。

**第一次跑建议**：先让它检查它自己。

```
用 verify-helper 检查 /绝对路径/verify-helper，fast=true
```

能返回一屏 PASS/FAIL 表格，就说明接对了。

---

## 工具栏按钮（可选，仅 DSH）

如果你用 **DeepSeek Harness**，`plugin/` 里有一个把验证变成按钮的小插件：

| 动作 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 单击 | 填入「快速检查」请求 |
| Shift + 单击 | 填入「完整检查」请求 |
| 双击 | 撤销，恢复点击前的草稿 |

它只把请求**写进输入框**（不自动发送），你改完按回车才跑。
安装方式见 [`plugin/README.md`](plugin/README.md)。其他 MCP 客户端用不到这个 —— 它们没有输入框工具栏。

---

## 检查项

由 [`check_specs.py`](check_specs.py) 生成，代码与文档不会漂移：

<!-- TABLE:START -->
| 检查 | 风险 | 阻断 | 判定什么 | 不通过怎么改 |
|---|---|:--:|---|---|
| `syntax` | 高 | ✅ | 每个 .py / .js / .json / .toml 文件都要能被对应的解析器接受。 | 按报错的行号修掉；JS 可用 node --check 单文件复现。 |
| `links` | 高 | ✅ | HTML 里的相对链接目标必须存在，页内与跨页锚点必须真实存在。 | 改链接指向真实文件，或补上被引用的 id；站点根绝对路径请用线上预览确认。 |
| `html` | 高 | ✅ | 标签必须配平（无孤立闭合、无未闭合），同一页面 id 不得重复。 | 补齐缺失的闭合标签；重复 id 改名并同步修改引用它的锚点。 |
| `secrets` | 严重 | ✅ | 源码与配置里不得出现真实凭据（API key、token、私钥、明文密码）。 | 立即吊销该凭据并改用环境变量；已提交历史也需清理。 |
| `encoding` | 高 | ✅ | 文本文件必须是合法 UTF-8（UTF-16 与 GBK 会被 Windows 工具链悄悄弄坏）。 | 转存为 UTF-8（无 BOM）；批量转换时注意先备份。 |
| `tests` | 高 | ✅ | 项目自带的测试套件必须真的跑起来并通过（以退出码为准）。 | 先修失败的用例；没有测试入口的话，至少补一个冒烟测试。 |
| `runtime-web` | 高 | ✅ | 静态站点的每个页面通过 HTTP 请求都必须返回 200（大小写、路径层级只有这一层能验出来）。 | 核对文件实际路径与链接大小写；确认站点根目录正确。 |
| `browser` | 高 | ✅ | 用真实浏览器打开每个页面，抓 JS 未捕获异常、console.error 与资源 404（需要本机装有 playwright）。 | 按报错栈修脚本；资源 404 通常是路径或大小写写错。 |
| `interaction` | 高 | ✅ | 按 verify.toml 的 [[flows]] 真的去点、填、选，再断言结果；未捕获异常一律算失败（需要 playwright）。 | 修失败的那一步：选择器写错就改选择器，点了没反应就查脚本。 |
| `a11y` | 低 | — | img 有 alt、单页一个 h1、有 title 与 lang、target=_blank 带 rel=noopener。 | 补 alt / 调整标题层级 / 加 lang；外链加 rel="noopener"。 |
| `bom` | 低 | — | 文件开头不应有 UTF-8 BOM（会让 CSS/JS 首行规则失效、diff 多一个隐形字符）。 | 用编辑器或脚本去掉开头的 EF BB BF 三字节。 |
| `paths` | 低 | — | 代码与文档里不应写死本机绝对路径（发布时会泄漏用户名与目录结构）。 | 改成相对路径或环境变量。 |
| `imports` | 低 | — | Python 里导入了却没用到的名字（会拖慢启动、掩盖真实依赖）。 | 删掉未使用的 import；若是再导出，加进 __all__ 或用 # noqa 说明。 |
| `todos` | 低 | — | 代码里 TODO / FIXME 的数量（只报告，不判定对错）。 | 要么做完，要么改成 issue 编号。 |
| `custom` | 中 | — | 项目 verify.toml 里声明的正则规则（规则即数据，不用改引擎）。 | 按规则里写的 message 修改。 |
| `mutation` | 中 | — | 把改动行里的运算符/布尔值改坏，重跑测试：测试还能通过，说明这行没有有效断言（opt-in，默认不跑）。 | 给这些行补上真正会失败的断言，或删掉死代码。 |
| `git` | 低 | — | 工作区是否有未提交改动（默认不参与总判定）。 | 确认这些改动是有意保留的，或提交/ stash 掉。 |
<!-- TABLE:END -->

**风险等级决定阻不阻断**：`严重` / `高` → 阻断（FAIL 会让总判定失败）；`中` / `低` → 只报告。

---

## 三态规则

```
PASS    检查跑了，且通过
FAIL    检查跑了，且不通过
UNKNOWN 没跑 / 跑不了 / 判不了 —— 永远不许当 PASS
```

另有一个 `applicable` 标志：项目里根本没有这类文件时（比如没有 HTML 却要查链接），
记 `UNKNOWN + applicable=false`，它**不参与总判定** —— 那是「不适用」，不是「判不了」。

总判定：

```
有阻断项 FAIL        → FAIL
否则有阻断项 UNKNOWN  → UNKNOWN
否则有阻断项 PASS     → PASS
只跑了非阻断检查      → UNKNOWN，并说明原因
```

这条规则的理论依据是测试领域的 **oracle 问题**：没有判定标准，跑再多遍也证明不了正确。

---

## 基线差分：这次比上次多了什么

```bash
python verify_core.py . --baseline save     # 存一份当前状态
# ……改代码……
python verify_core.py . --baseline check    # 与上次比
```

输出会多一段：

```
与基线相比：新增 1 条问题
  + [syntax] broken.py:1 invalid syntax
恶化的检查：syntax
```

指纹用「文件 + 消息」的哈希，所以**行号漂移不会误报**。基线文件是项目根的
`.verify-baseline.json`，建议加进 `.gitignore`。

## 变异门：测试到底有没有断言

覆盖率只说明「代码被执行到了」，不说明「断言有效」。变异门会把你的代码改坏，
再看测试能不能发现：

```bash
python verify_core.py . --checks mutation
```

```
✗ 变异门（中·不阻断） — 试了 1 个变异，被杀 0，存活 1
    · calc.py:2 把 + 改成 - 后测试仍然通过 —— 这行没有有效断言
```

规则：

- **只打 git diff 的行**，最多 5 个变异，每个 90 秒超时 —— 全量变异在小项目上也跑不动；
- 改完**立刻还原**源文件（`finally` 里还原，测试崩了也不会留坏代码）；
- 默认不跑（不在默认检查集里），要显式 `--checks mutation`；
- 没测试入口就记 UNKNOWN，不假装验过。

---

## 每条失败项带「往哪修」

报告里不只有「哪儿错了」，还有方向：

```
× 链接与锚点【高】 — 死链 1
    · notes/papers.html:205 死链：advising-rules.js
      方向：站点里没有 advising-rules.js 这个文件，但这一行在引用它 → 把这一行的引用改成
            真实存在的文件；如果文件名是构建时改掉的，改构建脚本，别改生成出来的页面
      别动：.verifyignore（加进去只是掩盖，不算修好） / 同页的其他链接
      验证：verify_start(checks=[links]) 应 PASS（命令行 --checks links）
```

**为什么需要这个**：只说「改链接指向真实文件」，模型能选的做法太多 ——
改链接？改文件名？建个空文件？删掉这页？加进 `.verifyignore`？
**每条都能让检查变绿，但只有一条是对的。**

### 四条硬规则

方向不是随便写的，四道闸任一不过就**不写**（宁缺勿滥）：

| 闸 | 要求 |
|---|---|
| 有证据 | 必须写出 `文件:行`，且真的出现在根因里 |
| 可验证 | 必须有一条能跑的 `--checks <id>` 命令 |
| 有边界 | 必须写明至少一条「不要动 X」 |
| 最小 | 不许出现「重写整个文件」「删掉测试」「关掉检查」 |

### 三种分类

| 类 | 含义 | 产出 |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | 有公认正确做法（死链、BOM、编码、未用 import） | 完整的改法 |
| **B** | 要你决定（凭据吊销、路径要不要改、h1 怎么排） | 只写「你要定什么」，**不给改法** |
| **C** | 不该修（TODO 统计、git 状态） | 不给方向 |

### 成本

`0` 次额外检查、`0` 次额外调用、`< 1ms` / 条 —— **总时长不变**。
通过的项一个字段都不加。

---

## 交互测试：真的点一下

`browser` 只证明「页面能打开」；**交互测试**证明「点了有反应」。

在 `verify.toml` 写几条用户会走的路：

```toml
[[flows]]
name = "升学自检：切标签 + 空输入应给提示"
steps = [
  { goto   = "notes/advising/index.html" },
  { click  = '[data-tab="report"]' },
  { expect = { selector = '[data-tab="report"][aria-selected="true"]', visible = true } },
  { fill   = '#targetAtar', value = '85' },
  { expect = { selector = '#targetAtar', input_value = '85' } },
  { click  = '#btnAtar' },
  { expect = { selector = '#atarBox', text_contains = '门' } },
  { expect = { no_console_error = true } },
]
```

```bash
python verify_core.py . --checks interaction
```

```
✓ 交互测试【高】 — 1 条流程，通过 1，失败 0（部署前缀 /ausmat-guide）  [2.68s]
```

失败时给到「第几步、什么动作、为什么」：

```
✗ 交互测试【高】 — 1 条流程，通过 0，失败 1
    · 故意写错选择器:2 「故意写错选择器」第 2 步 点击 #btnAtarTYPO 失败：
      page.click: Timeout 10000ms exceeded.
  证据在 C:\...\vh-flow-fqatw16p（失败截图留在里面）
```

**动作**：`goto` / `click` / `fill` / `select` / `press` / `wait` / `expect`（每步一个）

**断言**：`selector` + `visible` / `text_contains` / `input_value`；或 `url_contains`；
或 `no_console_error`；都可加 `timeout`

规则：

- **流程执行期间出现未捕获异常 → 整条失败**，不用你写断言
- 选择器写错会以「超时」报出来，不会静默通过
- 断言状态用属性选择器最稳：`'[data-tab="report"][aria-selected="true"]'`
- 需要 playwright；没有就记 UNKNOWN，不假装验过
- `--fast` 会跳过它

完整示例见 [`examples/verify-flows.toml`](examples/verify-flows.toml)。

---

## 自定义规则（规则即数据）

在项目根放 `verify.toml`，不改引擎就能加检查：

```toml
[[rules]]
id = "no-console-log"
pattern = 'console\.log\('
paths = ["**/*.js", "**/*.mjs"]
message = "生产代码里不要留 console.log"
risk = "medium"          # medium/low 只报告；high/critical 会让总判定 FAIL

[[rules]]
id = "no-http"
pattern = 'src="http://'
paths = ["**/*.html"]
message = "站内资源不要用 http://"
risk = "high"
```

## 排除文件

`.verifyignore`（一行一个 glob，`#` 注释），用来排除模板片段、页面快照、示例代码：

```
src/current-index.html
templates/**/*.html
```

**按目录生效**，和 `.gitignore` 一样：子项目里放自己的 `.verifyignore`，
从父目录扫整个工作区时它同样有效。

## 工作区会被提醒

如果一个目录下面识别到 ≥3 个子项目，报告里会明说：

```
注意：这看起来是**工作区**（识别到 4 个子项目）。工具不会替你挑项目，
     草稿、备份、资料都会被算进来。建议对单个项目跑，或先写 .verifyignore。
```

它**不会**替你猜哪个是项目 —— 猜错就会漏验。提醒你，但不替你做决定。

---

## SARIF 与 GitHub Code Scanning

```bash
python verify_core.py . --sarif verify.sarif
```

上传后，每条告警会直接出现在 PR 的 diff 行内。工作流示例见
[`examples/github-action.yml`](examples/github-action.yml)。

---

## 性能

不追求「全量」，追求「快到可以随手跑」：

| 项目规模 | 检查项 | 耗时 |
|---|---|---|
| 53 个文件 | 14 项 | 0.66s |
| 1,868 个文件 | 14 项 | 1.85s |
| 11,470 个文件 | 14 项 | **4.8s** |

做到这一点的四件事：

1. **合并扫描** —— 密钥 / 路径 / TODO / 编码 / BOM 五项共用一次逐行遍历；
2. **字面量预筛** —— 先在小写字节流里找 16 个标记（`sk-`、`password`、`TODO`…），一个都没有就完全不逐行扫；
3. **共享读缓存** —— 一份文件被多个检查读，只读一次；
4. **并行 + 缓存** —— 检查并行跑；`node --check` 结果按 `(mtime, size)` 缓存。

---

## 设计取舍

**保留的（我们的味道）**

- 三态而不是两态：`UNKNOWN` 是一等公民。
- 每条结论都带命令和退出码，可事后复核。
- 中文优先，输出给人看，不给人猜。
- 零第三方依赖，`git clone` 就能跑。

**抄来的（别人的精华）**

- 风险分级（OpenSSF Scorecard）：每项带 Critical/High/Medium/Low。
- 修复建议（Scorecard）：每条规则都有 remediation。
- SARIF（OASIS 标准）：结果能被 GitHub Code Scanning 直接消费。
- 规则即数据（Semgrep）：`verify.toml` 让用户加检查不改引擎。
- 配置生成文档（Scorecard）：README 的表格由 `check_specs.py` 生成。

**明确不做的（别人的糟粕）**

- ❌ 堆几百条规则 —— 规则越多越互相冲突，维护成本指数上升。
- ❌ 把覆盖率当唯一指标 —— 覆盖率说明「执行到」，不说明「断言有效」。
- ❌ 全量变异测试 —— 小项目也跑不动，只做静态 + 运行时。
- ❌ 用 LLM 评审当唯一闸门 —— 没有 oracle，正好是本工具要解决的问题。

---

## 局限（说清楚，不掩饰）

- **没有浏览器层**：`runtime-web` 只验 HTTP 200，抓不到 JS 报错、点击无反应、渲染错位。这是下一版（v1.2）的事。
- **没有变异测试**：只跑现有测试，不判断测试本身够不够强。
- **没有基线**：不做「这次比上次多了什么」的差分。
- **JS 语法检查单次上限 120 个文件**，超出会如实写「另有 N 个未检查」，不假装查过。
- **站点根绝对路径**（`/xxx`）离线不校验，只在报告里标注。

---

## 开发

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v     # 102 个单元测试
python conformance.py                       # 48 项符合性测试（喂整个项目进去）
python verify_core.py . --fast              # 自己检查自己
```

两套测试分工不同：

| | 单元测试（`tests/`） | 符合性测试（`conformance.py`） |
|---|---|---|
| 测什么 | 函数与规则的边界 | **喂一整个项目进去，结论对不对** |
| 怎么造 | 临时目录里的最小 fixture | 自己生成 32 个小项目 |
| 覆盖 | 解析、判定、渲染、MCP 协议 | 真阳性 / 假阳性抵抗 / 三态 / 刁难用例 / 输出契约 |
| 退出码 | unittest 的 | 非 0 = 有回归 |

`conformance.py` 的用例分六类：

1. **干净项目不能被冤枉** —— 最简包、空目录、只有 README
2. **每个检查抓到该抓的** —— 坏语法、死链、未闭合、假密钥、GBK、BOM、a11y、未用 import
3. **假阳性抵抗** —— 占位符路径、别人的路径、单引号 `href`、`.verifyignore`、`build/`
4. **三态规则** —— 只跑非阻断项 / 没源文件 / 拼错检查名，都必须是 UNKNOWN
5. **刁难它** —— 外链、`mailto:`、`#锚点`、坏 TOML、CRLF、0 字节文件、
   中文加空格文件名、非法 UTF-8、嵌套 ignore、3MB 大文件
6. **输出契约** —— SARIF、`--json`、`--sarif`、幂等、方向卡四段、退出码语义（含 fail-closed）

测试不依赖任何本机真实项目：所有 fixture 在临时目录里现造、跑完即删。

## 许可证

MIT

---

## 分层闸门（v1.9）

v1.9 之前，它是一次性跑 15 项、给一个 PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN。
现在多了**生命周期语义**：这一轮属于哪层、这次改动多危险、哪些问题被谁回应了。

### 1. 分层：`--stage`

| 层 | 该拦什么 | 跑哪些检查 |
|---|---|---|
| `precommit` | 秒级反馈，挂 git hook | syntax / encoding / bom / secrets / imports / paths / todos / custom |
| `pr` | 完整静态 + 运行时 | 默认全部 |
| `merge` | 与目标分支组合后全量再跑 | 默认全部（配 `--against main`） |
| `postdeploy` | 只验线上行为 | runtime-web / browser / interaction / tests |

```bash
python verify_core.py . --stage precommit      # 提交前，亚秒级
python verify_core.py . --stage pr             # PR
python verify_core.py . --stage merge --against main   # 合并队列
```

### 2. 风险档：`--tier auto`

**由变更决定，不由项目决定**。命中敏感路径（auth/、billing/、.github/workflows/、
migrations/、installer、*.pem…）或改动 ≥400 行 / ≥25 文件 → `high`（要 2 人）；
≥60 行或 ≥6 文件 → `medium`（1 人）；其余 `low`（0 人）。

### 3. 每条 finding 必须被回应

```bash
# 修掉，或者写理由接受（会落盘到 .verify-accept.json，可入库、可审计）
python verify_core.py . --accept "bom:a.py:1:3c7f56dfc6::构建会重新生成，已确认"
```
- **凭据类（secrets）永远不接受**，必须真修。
- 只有**中风险及以上**未回应才会卡住合并；低风险只提示（避免噪声把人逼到无视它）。

### 4. 噪声与收敛

每轮记录 finding 集合，算 `新增 / 重复 / 修好`；**连续三轮条数不变 → 判定收敛**，
提示「剩下的要么接受要么改，不要再刷第 4 轮」。
`--only-new` 可只看本轮新出现的问题。

### 5. 回归集：`regression.toml`

```toml
[[case]]
path = "src/app.py"
check = "syntax"
why = "曾经少个括号，整站白屏"
```

每次运行都会检查这些「出过事的路径」有没有被覆盖到、对应检查有没有真的跑到。

### 6. 安全层

在 `secrets` 之上再扫一遍危险调用（`shell=True`、`eval/exec`、`os.system`、
明文 `http://`、关闭 TLS 校验…）。**只有凭据类（critical）直接阻塞**；
高危项进入「未回应」清单，必须修或写理由接受。

### 7. 证据留档

失败/未知项的**命令、退出码、原始输出、findings** 落到
`.verify-artifacts/<时间戳>/`（只保留最近 20 次）。
报告里给目录与文件数 —— 下一个人不用重跑，也不用相信"我看过了"。

### 8. REVIEW.md

仓库可以放一份 `REVIEW.md` 告诉检查器这个仓库的规矩：

```
skip: drafts/**, legacy/**
no-style: true          # 只关 a11y 这类纯风格项
require-evidence: true  # 没有 file:line 的 finding 直接丢
max-nits: 2
fail-means: 文档说谎
```

### 9. 度量

报告里带 `metrics`：`unknown_rate`（缺 oracle 的比例）、
`needs_human_eyes`（需要人看的条数，用来代理"人的时间"）、
`noise_new/repeat/fixed`、`slowest` 三项。

### 10. MCP 工具

新增 `verify_accept`（list / add / clear），`verify_start` 的 schema 也带上了
`stage / tier / accept / only_new / against / artifacts / review_md`。

# dsh-web-tool-provider

DeepSeek Harness 的 `web_search` / `web_fetch` 与 **Tavily / Exa / Firecrawl** 之间的**归一化中间层**。

```text
web_search ─┐                          ┌─ tavily
            ├─ ctx.web 统一契约 ───────┤
web_fetch  ─┘   （本插件负责转换）        └─ exa / firecrawl
```

- **输入归一**：通用层只有条数、深度、域名白/黑名单；厂商独占的项留在各自的卡片里（例如只有 Tavily 有「合成答案」）。每个 adapter 负责翻译，厂商做不到的**以 notice 告知模型**，装死不是选项。
- **输出归一**：一个 source 形状、一种日期格式、一套错误码；厂商的 `author`/`warnings`/`failed_results` 都折进同一处。

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:nhhc-lxr/dsh-web-tool-provider
```

## 设置页

**Settings → Plugins → 网页工具后端**，三层结构：

```text
┌ API 密钥 ──────────────────────────┐   三家各一行，存进凭据库
├ [搜索 web_search] [抓取 web_fetch] ┤   两个 tab，互不干扰
│  通用参数                          │   条数 / 深度 / 黑白域名
│  Tavily   Exa   Firecrawl          │   各自一张卡：接口地址、超时、正文上限，
└────────────────────────────────────┘   + 该家在该 tab 下的特色项
```

- 每个 tab 顶部是「通用参数」，**只放三家都认的东西**：条数、域名白/黑名单；深度算半通用（Tavily/Exa 有，Firecrawl 没有，会发 notice）。
- 每张 provider 卡片有自己的接口地址、超时、正文上限，以及该家独有的项（Tavily 的 `topic`/`searchDepth`/**`answer`**、Exa 的 `searchType`、Firecrawl 的 `version`/`mainContent`/`maxAge`）。
- 卡片右上角是「使用中」标记；点「设为该工具后端」即切换，下一次调用生效。
- 不支持的通用选项按当前后端标 `支持 / 不支持`，运行时以 `> provider notice: ...` 告知模型，**不会让调用失败**。

密钥解析顺序：插件配置里的字面量 → 凭据库 → 环境变量（`TAVILY_API_KEY` / `EXA_API_KEY` / `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`），每次调用重新解析。**字面量密钥不会被写进状态文件。**

## 配置（YAML 也可以）

| 层 | 字段 |
|---|---|
| `search` | `backend`、`maxResults`、`depth`(auto/fast/balanced/deep)、`includeDomains`、`excludeDomains` |
| `fetch` | `backend`、`fallbackToHttp` |
| `providers.tavily` | `baseURL`、`timeoutMs`、`maxChars`、`topic`、`searchDepth`、`answer`、`apiKey`、`apiKeyEnv` |
| `providers.exa` | `baseURL`、`timeoutMs`、`maxChars`、`searchType`、`apiKey`、`apiKeyEnv` |
| `providers.firecrawl` | `baseURL`、`timeoutMs`、`maxChars`、`version`、`mainContent`、`maxAge`、`apiKey`、`apiKeyEnv` |

设置存在插件自管状态文件（`<profile>/.web-tool-provider/state.json`，回退 `$DSH_HOME`、`~/.dsh`）；YAML 里的 `Config` 只是首次运行的默认值，状态文件优先。

## 输出契约

```ts
SearchResult = { content?: string; sources: { url; title?; snippet?; publishedAt? }[]; truncated: boolean }
FetchResult  = { url: string; statusCode: number; body: { kind: 'text' | 'html'; content: string }; truncated: boolean }
```

- `snippet` 单行、≤400 字；`author` 以 ` · 作者` 附在末尾；`highlights` 数组拼成一段。
- `publishedAt` 一律 `YYYY-MM-DD`。
- `content` = 「厂商答案 + notices」；抓取降级也会附 `> provider notice: fell back ...`。
- 错误码：`WEB_PROVIDER_UNAUTHORIZED` / `_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` / `_RATE_LIMITED` / `_BAD_REQUEST` / `_UPSTREAM` / `_UNREACHABLE` / `_EMPTY` / `_CREDENTIAL_MISSING`、`WEB_ABORTED`、`WEB_INVALID_URL`、`WEB_BLOCKED_URL`。

## 行为

- **`web_search` 多 query = 多次厂商调用**（工具层并发 fan-out 后合并）。在意额度就调小 `dsh-tool-web` 的 `searchMaxQueries`。
- **抓取结果一律 `text`**：三家给的都是 markdown，标成 `html` 会让工具层再转一遍。
- **抓取降级**：厂商报错/额度/无密钥/空正文/超时 → 本地抓取并附带 notice；目标页 4xx 是结果不降级；abort 不降级。
- **搜索不降级**：选中的后端没配密钥就报 `WEB_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_MISSING`，提示去设置页。

本地抓取只做协议白名单、明文内网/回环地址拦截、逐跳重定向校验与字节上限，**没有**官方 `dsh-web-fetch-http` 的 DNS 解析+公网校验+连接钉扎。要那层保护就关掉 `fallbackToHttp`。

## 隐私

用 Tavily / Exa / Firecrawl 时查询词与目标 URL 会发给对应厂商；本地降级路径不经过第三方。

## 开发

- `index.js`：分层设置 + 归一化层 + 两个 provider + 两条 Host 路由，零第三方依赖。
- `client.js`：设置页（两个 tab + 三家卡片），`window.__ModuleLoader__` 模块，注册进 `settings.plugins.tab`。
- `node test/smoke.mjs`：21 项离线测试（同形输出、旋钮翻译、notice、错误分类、降级开关、分层持久化、密钥隔离）。

> 装完或改完代码需要**重启一次** Harness：模块缓存不会因为重新安装而失效。

## License

MIT

No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-claude-provider

A **Settings → Providers** panel for Anthropic **Claude Code / Claude Pro / Max** in
DeepSeek Harness, so a Claude subscription can pay for inference instead of an API key.

## What this adds

DeepSeek Harness can already run Anthropic's OAuth login — `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai`
registers an authorization flow for every pi-ai catalog provider it can sign in,
`anthropic` included. What it shipped without is a surface: nothing in the UI called
`ctx.authorization.begin()` for anything except the DeepSeek account.

This plugin is that surface. It renders a Providers section, lists the registered
Anthropic flow and its methods, runs an attempt, shows the authorization URL and any
code the flow reports, relays the flow's questions (login method, pasted code) to the
panel, and reports whether a credential is stored.

It does **not** reimplement OAuth. PKCE, the loopback callback server, the pasted-code
fallback, the token exchange, rotating refresh, and the Claude Code identity headers
(`anthropic-beta: claude-code-…`, `oauth-2025-04-20`, the `claude-cli/…` user agent)
all stay in pi-ai and the harness adapter, which means they keep getting fixed upstream.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:ObnubiladO/dsh-claude-provider
```

Restart DeepDive, then open **Settings → Providers**.

## Sign in

1. **Sign in with Claude** starts an attempt.
2. The panel shows the authorization URL — Anthropic's current entry point
   `https://claude.com/cai/oauth/authorize`, which redirects to `claude.ai/oauth/authorize`.
   Open it, approve, and finish in the browser.
3. If the browser cannot reach the local callback (remote machine, container), choose the
   pasted-code method and paste the code Claude shows.

The credential lands in the harness credential store as the `llm-pi-ai/anthropic` grant
record, which is exactly where the adapter looks, so no route configuration is needed.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness / DeepDive with `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-authorization` mounted
- Verified against `dsh 0.2.1-rc.3` (DeepDive 0.2.7)

## Files

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/index.js` | host plugin: a `TypertRemoteService` (`claudeProvider`) that bridges `ctx.authorization` to the browser |
| `lib/client.js` | client plugin: the Providers panel (`settings.section`) |

## License

MIT.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
dsh-mnemon

English · 简体中文

Composable, view-based context for DeepSeek Harness.

Pluggable sources and strategies, with layered memory and self-evolving skills out of the box.

Install and start · Watch the demo · Documentation · Build a plugin

## Why dsh-mnemon An Agent that starts every session from scratch keeps asking what it was already told. Putting everything into one memory store is no better: it either floods each turn or misses what matters. dsh-mnemon gives DeepSeek Harness memory that is layered, visible and composable, and skills that improve with use. - **The right memory for each turn.** Preferences and working facts stay in context. Project documents and long-term evidence are searched only when a question needs them. - **You can see what a turn used.** Under each reply, the turn memory bar lists the documents and memories the turn read and wrote, and one click opens each in the Memory System. The Memory System shows everything that is stored and lets you edit it. - **Save to memory in one click.** When a conversation turns up a fact worth keeping, the brain mark under the reply hands it to a task Agent, which removes duplicates, distils it and writes it to the right Memory Space, or saves it where you choose: working memory, your profile or a Memory Space. The receipt says where it went. - **Skills that improve with use.** Skills keeps every DSH skill in one place. It can review your real conversations, draft a better `SKILL.md` and backtest it before you adopt it, and it installs more skills from skills.sh, GitHub and sites that publish Agent Skills. - **Compose it on the Plugins page.** Choose a main strategy and optional enhancements, and switch them without moving any data. Every component has its own page for its settings. - **Keep data where you want it.** Local by default with Mnemon Native, or one of eight third-party Providers. Storage can be global, per workspace, centralized or in a directory you choose, with ZIP backup. - **Extend it.** Sources and Strategies are ordinary DSH plugins built on public SDKs. An installed component gets the same pages and switches as the shipped ones. ## See it in action These recordings come from a real WebUI with the live DeepSeek model answering, on a seeded, fictional project, Lumen. Waits for the model play faster, marked in the lower right corner. **Save a new fact to memory.** A reply reports a new measurement. Select the brain mark under it, cut the candidate down to the sentence worth keeping and send it to the task Agent; the receipt names the Memory Space it went to and opens it in one click.

**See all memory in one place.** Status, runtime memory, Project Documents and Memory Spaces live in the Memory System. The graph links memories through the entities they mention, and Ask Agent answers with the memories it cites, by content.

**Compose memory on the Plugins page.** One main strategy, its memory sources and optional enhancements, each switch applying at once. Every component has its own page, and storage, backup and interface settings live here too.

Every step is explained in the [UI guide](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/ui-guide.md); all screens, recordings and the capture environment are in the [v0.5.32 gallery](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/assets/webui-v0.5.32/README.md). ## Three kinds of memory | Memory | Keep here | How it reaches the Agent | |---|---|---| | **Runtime memory** | Preferences, working agreements, facts needed on the next turn | Injected every turn as compact USER.md and MEMORY.md | | **Project Documents** | Designs, investigations, procedures and handoffs | Searched first, then read when relevant | | **Memory Spaces** | Durable facts, decisions, entities and their relationships | Recalled on demand from the enabled Providers | The default **Layered strategy** keeps runtime memory resident and reads the other two on demand. The **General strategy** offers every available source within one budget and lets the model decide how to use each. A **memory space** is one named, Provider-backed scope for long-term evidence; the Chinese product term is 记忆空间. ## Skills that improve with use **Skills** is an experimental component for the `SKILL.md` skills DSH loads from your project and your home folder. Its page sits in the Memory System, or in the sidebar on its own. | A turn's review suggests an improvement | You adopt it after a backtest | |---|---| | [![The Turn skills line under a reply: release-notes, suggested 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/main/docs/assets/skills-v0.5.34/en/chat-skills.jpg)](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/skills.md#in-a-conversation) | [![A draft of release-notes with its backtest, Current 40 → Draft 93 +53, and the diff](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/main/docs/assets/skills-v0.5.34/en/skills-draft.jpg)](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/skills.md#evolution) | - **Manage.** Switch a skill off for the model or the `/` menu, use it in the conversation in one click, edit it, and go back to any earlier version. - **Evolve.** With self-evolution on, finished conversations are reviewed in the background for corrections, "from now on" instructions, failed tools and reusable procedures. A suggestion cites the steps it rests on; a task Agent drafts the new `SKILL.md`, which is backtested against the current version before you adopt it. Nothing changes without your **Adopt**. - **Test.** Each skill has its own cases, from reviews, from recorded conversations or written by hand, and a backtest scores any version on them. - **Install.** The market searches skills.sh's open index and reads any GitHub repository, any site publishing an Agent Skills discovery index, and curated catalogs; every install is previewed, with security reviews where they exist. - **In the conversation.** A line under each turn names the skills it used and what its review suggested, each one click from its page. Self-evolution stays off until you turn it on under **Plugins → dsh-mnemon → Skills**. The [Skills guide](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/skills.md) walks through every screen. ## Quick start DSH loads the bundled `cordis.patch.yml` automatically. Do not copy its `insert` block into your profile: duplicate Mnemon entries prevent Settings from saving. See [manual-installation recovery](docs/en/guides/installation.md#settings-cannot-save-after-manual-installation) if you already copied it. New to DSH? [Install and start](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/installation.md) walks from an empty machine to your first memory, with a screenshot for every step. The short version, with [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 22.19 or later: ```sh npm install --global pnpm npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web ```

1. In the page that opens, click **Plugins → Add plugin**, type `dsh-mnemon`, click **Install**, then **Enable now**. 2. Open **Memory System** in the sidebar. **Status** shows each memory component and Provider. 3. Tell a conversation something to remember. The turn memory bar under the reply lists what the turn read and wrote, and the brain mark saves a reply to memory. 4. For Memory Spaces, install the Mnemon CLI for Mnemon Native with `npm install --global @mnemon-dev/mnemon`, or enable another Provider on the Memory Spaces page. 5. Choose the main strategy and enhancements under **Plugins → dsh-mnemon**. dsh-mnemon supports DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` (npm `latest` and `next`) and `0.2.0-rc.2`. The same package serves the desktop app's Plugins page, `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-mnemon` on the command line, and Headless with `dsh plugin --profile headless add dsh-mnemon`; older hosts keep the release [compatibility and upgrades](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/reference/compatibility.md) names for them. [Getting started](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/getting-started.md) continues from here, and [compatibility and upgrades](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/reference/compatibility.md) covers existing installations. ## How it works [![Source facts flow through a Strategy and Core validation into one View for the DSH Host](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/main/docs/assets/diagrams/en/composable-memory.png)](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/development/architecture.md) - **Sources** own memory and its operations: Runtime memory, Project Documents and Memory Spaces, whose Providers are its children. - A **Strategy** decides how the available Sources take part in a turn: what stays resident, what can be searched, and which tools and budgets apply. Enhancements add to it through standard slots. - **Core** validates the result into one immutable **View** for the turn. The DSH Host pins it to that turn and controls tool access. The same public contracts serve the shipped plugins and external repositories. [Architecture](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/development/architecture.md) explains ownership, the turn lifecycle and the UI regions components contribute to. ## Official plugins The Starter pins a tested combination of independently versioned packages. One main strategy runs at a time; the enhancements are off until you turn them on. | Package | Role | Default | |---|---|---| | [dsh-mnemon-source-runtime](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-source-runtime/README.md) | Runtime memory: USER.md, MEMORY.md, revisions and local storage | On | | [dsh-mnemon-source-documents](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-source-documents/README.md) | Project Documents: Markdown, search, revisions and archiving | On | | [dsh-mnemon-source-memory-spaces](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-source-memory-spaces/README.md) | Memory Spaces: durable evidence and their Providers | On | | [dsh-mnemon-source-skills](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-source-skills/README.md) | Skills (experimental): DSH skills with versions, self-evolution from real conversations, tests and backtests, and a market of skills.sh, GitHub and Agent Skills sites | On (self-evolution off) | | [dsh-mnemon-strategy-default-three-tier](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-strategy-default-three-tier/README.md) | Layered strategy: resident runtime memory, the rest on demand | Selected | | [dsh-mnemon-strategy-general](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-strategy-general/README.md) | General strategy: every available source in one budget | Off | | [dsh-mnemon-strategy-auto-capture](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-strategy-auto-capture/README.md) | Active capture: in-turn guidance to keep useful facts | Off | | [dsh-mnemon-strategy-light-context](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-strategy-light-context/README.md) | Light context: a shared ceiling on resident context | Off | | [dsh-mnemon-strategy-scoped](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-strategy-scoped/README.md) | Scoped composition: ordered sources and a writable subset | Off | Memory Spaces Providers: [Mnemon Native](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-provider-mnemon-native/README.md) (default, local) · [OpenViking](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-provider-openviking/README.md) · [Honcho](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-provider-honcho/README.md) · [Mem0](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-provider-mem0/README.md) · [Hindsight](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-provider-hindsight/README.md) · [Holographic](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-provider-holographic/README.md) · [RetainDB](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-provider-retaindb/README.md) · [ByteRover](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-provider-byterover/README.md) · [Supermemory](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/plugins/dsh-mnemon-provider-supermemory/README.md). Third-party Providers stay off until configured; graph, deletion and enumeration capabilities differ by backend. See [Providers](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/memory-providers.md). ## Build your own Define a Source or Strategy with `dsh-mnemon/extension-sdk`, add an enhancement through the standard slots, or write a Memory Spaces driver with `dsh-mnemon-source-memory-spaces/provider-sdk`. A component can also add its own settings and Status card to the pages dsh-mnemon shows. Your repository owns its manifest, dependencies, tests and build; DSH installs and mounts it, and choosing it as the main strategy is a separate decision. Start with the [plugin author guide](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/development/extensions.md). Discuss new capabilities and Providers in an Issue before a pull request; see [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Data and trust - Runtime memory and Project Documents are local files; Mnemon Native is local. Third-party Providers use their own services and scopes. - Turning a component off does not erase its memory, and changing the storage location does not move data. Use ZIP backup to carry it. - Skills keeps its evolution data (suggestions, test cases and the conversations reviews read, with secrets redacted) in the local storage root, outside backups. An Agent follows a skill from the market as written, so preview it before installing. - Git sync publishes the same Mnemon Pack payload as readable files to a repository you own, so another machine can pull it, with **Sync now**, **Check remote** before anything is written, or **Automatic sync**. When two machines wrote one subject differently, both wordings stay until you accept and apply a **Memory reconciliation** plan; see [Git repository sync](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/operations.md#git-repository-sync). - Saved Provider credentials stay on the Host and are never exported. Backups still contain private memory; protect them. - Sources and Strategies are trusted in-process JavaScript, not sandboxed code. Remembered history never outranks current instructions. [Backup and recovery](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/guides/operations.md) · [Security policy](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/SECURITY.md) · [Release history](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/releases/README.md) · [Roadmap](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/roadmap.md) ## Develop and verify ```sh pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm verify pnpm verify:plugins ``` Use Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` and pnpm. `node scripts/serve-e2e.mjs` starts a disposable real WebUI; add `--docs-demo` for the seeded project behind these screenshots, and `--live-model` to have the DeepSeek API answer, with the key read from `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. Mechanical tests are not claims about model accuracy or live cloud Providers. [Development and verification](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/docs/en/development/README.md). ## Star History ## License [MIT](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/LICENSE). Third-party providers keep their own licenses and terms; see [Third-party notices](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-mnemon/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
